item.title: State-selective dynamical freezing in driven Rydberg atom chains
item.description: arXiv:2611.28215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamical freezing, the near-complete suppression of dynamics at special drive frequencies, offers a route to mitigating Floquet heating in periodically driven quantum systems. In interacting systems, however, the energy cost of each transition depends on the many-body configuration, so that the freezing condition itself becomes state dependent. We study this dependence in periodically driven Rydberg atom chains under single- and bi-frequency driving. Using Floquet perturbation theory, we show that each spin flip is characterised by a single interference amplitude set by its local interaction shift, and that a state freezes only where the amplitudes of all its available flips vanish simultaneously. This picture accounts quantitatively for the shift and proliferation of freezing frequencies with interatomic spacing and for the response of entire families of initial states, which are sorted by a single local motif. Freezing is strong only within a window of spacings bounded by interaction tails on one side and nearest-neighbour excitation facilitation on the other, outside of which the advantage of bi-frequency driving is lost. In the regime of large detuning amplitude, where freezing points are numerous and the perturbative description is controlled, this window leaves almost no room for the PXP limit.
item.dc:creator: Madhumita Sarkar, Sougato Bose, Roopayan Ghosh

item.title: Foliated surface codes for optimal skip-gate leakage correction
item.description: arXiv:2611.28219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skip-gate leakage --- such as atom loss in neutral-atom arrays or trapped ions, or photon loss in superconducting dual-rail qubits --- takes a qubit out of its computational subspace and removes subsequent gates acting on it. If leakage is only detectable end-of-the-line at qubit measurement, error correction circuits must be designed to periodically measure all qubits, as in SWAP-based circuits and foliation. We show that the best SWAP-based surface code, although optimal against space-like skip-gate leakage errors, is suboptimal against time-like leakage errors. By optimal, we mean that the code corrects as many leakage errors as it can detect. Remarkably, we find that the foliated surface code is optimal against both space- and time-like error configurations. We support our findings with numerical simulations. Under two-qubit gate leakage with probability 0.5%, foliation suppresses time-like errors in a distance-4 rotated stability experiment by 1380(50) per two added rounds, compared to 63(1) for the best SWAP-based circuit. In memory, the two are comparable. Under an experimentally motivated neutral-atom noise model, we find that foliation outperforms SWAP-based circuits in stability for both rotated and unrotated code geometries. This holds true for a parameter sweep that takes the neutral-atom noise model from being dominated by computational errors to atom loss. Interestingly, a SWAP-based circuit for unrotated code memory performs best when computational noise dominates over loss. Our work motivates co-designing error correction circuits with logical operations: preferring foliation when time-like errors dominate and SWAP-based circuits when space-like errors dominate.
item.dc:creator: Runjiang Bi, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Thomas B. Smith, Margaret Pavlovich, Ming Li, Shruti Puri

item.title: Mitigating large circuits with a learned small-circuit mitigator
item.description: arXiv:2611.28261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning-based quantum error mitigation infers noise-free results from noisy measurement data. However, exact training labels become prohibitively expensive to compute as circuits grow, and the generalization capability of a trained model to infer accurate results on circuits of depths and sizes it was not trained on poses a challenge. We show that circuit cutting allows such a model to be reused on circuits larger than those it was trained on. We benchmark this approach against zero-noise extrapolation, Clifford data regression, and probabilistic error cancellation on simulated circuits several times wider and deeper than the training circuits. On random-circuit chains, the fragment-wise mitigator removes most of the reconstructed error. For a holographic Ising-chain eigensolver under a fixed shot budget, it recovers most of the noise-induced energy error, close to 90\% or more, and outperforms Clifford data regression and probabilistic error cancellation. Since the mitigator is trained once and needs no additional circuits or noise amplification at inference, its cost is paid up front rather than for every new circuit. The approach is also modular. Any improvement to the small-circuit mitigator, such as retraining on larger fragments or on device-specific noise, carries over directly to every circuit that can be cut into such fragments. Our proposal thus offers a practical route to bringing learned error mitigation to quantum computations far beyond the reach of exact training labels, provided they can be partitioned with a moderate number of cuts.
item.dc:creator: Thi Ha Kyaw, Pablo D\'iez-Valle, Gaurav Saxena

item.title: Comment on phase vortex lattices in neutron interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.28316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a phase-based theoretical description of the four-plate crystal neutron interferometer (LLLL geometry) originally introduced by Heinrich et al. [Z. Phys. B 72, 357 (1988)]. The LLLL interferometer can be interpreted as two coupled LLL interferometric loops that share partial beam paths, leading to characteristic interference phenomena beyond the standard three-plate configuration. Using a coherent beam-splitting model we derive the forward intensity in terms of loop phase sums and recover the cosine-sum structure reported in Refs.[1,2]. Based on these results we analyze the phase dependence of the forward beam in the presence of localized phase objects, such as wedges inserted into individual partial beams. In experiments presented in [2], the LLLL interferometer is used to generate a periodic array of intensity in two dimensions by which the authors claim to demonstrate a phase vortex grating of significant extrinsic orbital angular momentum (OAM). However, the same interference patterns are predicted by simulating a coherent superposition of {beam paths} along different interferometer loops and experiencing phase shifts in each loop due to two wedges that are perpendicular to each other, without assuming any neutron OAM.
item.dc:creator: Wolfgang Treimer, Terrence Jach, Martin suda, Frank Hau{\ss}er

item.title: Distant Bell States via Measured Spin Chain Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.28325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preparing distant qubits in Bell states is a core requirement for quantum networking and distributed quantum computation. The nonequilibrium unitary dynamics of spin chains have been envisaged as a convenient quantum channel for intra-chip communications. Typically it establishes mixed entangled states between its remote ends, to be purified by entanglement distillation after several uses of the channel to obtain Bell states. Here we show how the establishment of entanglement via spin chain dynamics can be (a) sped up and (b) made to yield a pure entangled state after a single usage of the channel, which is upgradable to a Bell-state without the complexity of purification. To this end, we intersperse unitary evolution for some period with measurements on intermediary spins. We explore two different measurements: a measurement that post-selects for a ground state; and local measurements in the computational basis. We illustrate the mechanism with qubits coupled to the ends of a 1D $XY$ spin chain.
item.dc:creator: Ralph Jason Costales, Sougato Bose

item.title: Tailored Magic States for Algorithmic Primitives
item.description: arXiv:2611.28353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Algorithmic primitives such as adders, multipliers, and Boolean logic typically contain clusters of multi-qubit non-Clifford gates, whose decomposition into $T$ and $CCZ$ gates adds scheduling and spacetime overhead in fault-tolerant quantum computers. Synthillation addresses this difficulty for diagonal circuits at the third level of the Clifford hierarchy by jointly synthesizing and distilling their non-Clifford content. In this work, we develop a complementary, code-theoretic approach to synthillation. We introduce CSS-T-Product (CSS-TP) codes, whose transversal single-qubit phase gates implement multi-qubit logical diagonal gates, and give analytical rules that predict these logical gates from tensor-network operations. Using quantum LEGO, we generate code families with logical actions at the third and fourth levels of the Clifford hierarchy. We classify the resulting resource states as canonical (such as $T$ or $CCZ$), tensor products of canonical states, or irreducible, i.e., not reducible to a product of non-Clifford gates via Clifford operations and logical basis changes. Conversion into Encode-$T$-Decode factories built from these codes recover known synthillation resources and prepare magic states at higher levels of the Clifford hierarchy; we analyze them with a surface-code-based model for several algorithmic primitives. We demonstrate that tailored magic factories give significant latency improvements at similar or smaller occupied spacetime volume: at code distance $21$ with one factory per resource family, they reduce the latency of a $GF(2^{8})$ multiplier and a shared-addend carry-lookahead adder by up to $48\%$ and $38\%$, respectively, and the smallest tailored factory also lowers the occupied spacetime volume. CSS-TP codes thus connect code construction to resource factories for specific algorithmic primitives.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Steinberg, Joseph Sullivan, Chunjun Cao, Michael Perlin

item.title: Incompressible quantum information
item.description: arXiv:2611.28361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a small classical system correlated with a large one, it is always possible to compress the large system down to a size only dependent on the size of the smaller one, while preserving all correlations up to a given controllable error. Here, we show that such a statement does not hold at all when the large system is quantum mechanical. More precisely, we show that there are bipartite states such that any compression of the large system, by a non-trivial relative factor, will necessarily lead to the destruction of a significant amount of correlation, measured in mutual information. Our results therefore identify a limitation of information-bottleneck approaches to quantum machine learning, showing that a small system specifying the relevant features contained in a large quantum data set does not guarantee a compact encoding of the latter that preserves the relevant correlations.
item.dc:creator: Lasse H. Wolff, Matthias Christandl, Bergfinnur Durhuus, Christoph Hirche, Andreas Winter

item.title: Online Scheduling for Entanglement Distillation: Learning When to Wait
item.description: arXiv:2611.28373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entanglement distillation probabilistically increases the fidelity of entangled pairs at the cost of reducing their number. The outcome of each distillation operation takes time to communicate, during which the entangled pairs decohere while idle in their memories. This raises a dilemma: wait for the outcome before proceeding, or continue optimistically at the risk of needlessly consuming further pairs. We study online distillation scheduling, in which distillation trees are constructed dynamically to maximize the throughput of pairs that meet a required fidelity. A policy decides which pairs to distill together and, for each operation, whether to wait for its outcome. We derive an upper bound on the throughput of every scheduling policy and, by formulating the problem as a Markov decision process, train, with reinforcement learning, a policy that applies to any number of memories. Compared with two baselines that always or never wait, the learned policy delivers as many pairs of the required fidelity as the better one when one of these two extremes is the best choice, and more otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Panagiotis Promponas, Spyros Tserkis, Leandros Tassiulas

item.title: Verification and Evaluation of A Comprehensive Quantum Simulation Compiler
item.description: arXiv:2611.28388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hamiltonian simulation is a central application of quantum computing, yet most existing compilers offer no machine-checked guarantee that the circuits they produce approximate the intended evolution. The previous QBlue compiler verifies a Hamiltonian simulation compiler containing only Trotter-based algorithms. It takes a Hamiltonian written over Pauli strings, a simulation time, and an error bound, and produces a circuit or analog schedule that is proven, in the Rocq proof assistant, to approximate the ideal time evolution within that bound and proves a single end-to-end error bound that composes the errors of the individual stages; the compiler uses it to select, by resource estimation, the cheapest algorithm that meets the user's bound. This paper advances the verification efforts with two further steps. First, we extend QBlue to $\textsf{QBlue}_{\texttt{BE}}$ by verifying another important compilation method for Hamiltonian simulation: block-encoding-based (BE-based) algorithms. Second, we empirically evaluate 279 Hamiltonian simulation programs against the state-of-the-art BE-based compiler, PennyLane. For many programs, our compiler shows a $94\%$ gate reduction compared to PennyLane. Additionally, we also discover issues and bugs in PennyLane. We also compare Trotter- and BE-based algorithms, providing a practical comparison for the long-standing debate over which algorithms perform better. Our results surprisingly show that Trotter-based algorithms may gain a practical advantage, even though BE algorithms have a theoretical advantage.
item.dc:creator: Bhuwan Joshi, Zoukarneini Difaizi Tagba, Zhi Xiang Chong, Liyi Li

item.title: Froq: Safe Speculative Execution on Live Quantum States for FTQC
item.description: arXiv:2611.28427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reducing execution time is critical to fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) as longer executions expose logical qubits to more opportunities for failure. However, quantum processors could frequently stall due to slow classical error-correction decoders. Recent speculative decoding accelerates this process, but its speculation remains on the classical side, leaving quantum operations waiting for confirmed decoding results. Extending speculative execution to the quantum side is fundamentally challenging. Unlike classical processor states, quantum states cannot be arbitrarily copied or checkpointed for rollback, making recovery from mispredictions difficult. In this work, we propose Froq to enable safe speculative execution on live quantum states. Froq uses compiler-assisted recovery contracts to track how mispredictions propagate through quantum operations. It further employs a resource-aware runtime mechanism to reserve recovery workspace and dynamically balance the benefits of speculative execution against the expected costs of recovery. We evaluate Froq on eight FTQC programs across 88 configurations, building on an existing speculative window decoder. Froq reduces quantum-side time by 9.81% across all 88 configurations. The reduction reaches 18.34% across the 45 configurations allowing concurrent predictions, and peaks at 31.1% at code distance d=21, under limited resources.
item.dc:creator: Yicheng Guang, Yueqi Chen

item.title: Causal Consistency and Cost of Quantum Control
item.description: arXiv:2611.28478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An unknown quantum state can supply the information needed to control a computation, but how much quantum data must be consumed to perform a prescribed action? We connect this resource question to causal consistency within the quantum state space. No-signaling requires identical observable predictions for remotely chosen ensemble preparations of the same complete input; quantum distinguishability then converts this requirement into finite-copy bounds. For amplitude amplification, we identify an exact low-copy obstruction and establish a dimension-independent, optimal quadratic dependence of the copy cost on angular gain at fixed accuracy, uniformly over arbitrary pure inputs. A coherent protocol attains this scaling without reconstructing a classical state description. Prior knowledge of a real two-level family additionally permits exponentially decreasing error with the copy budget at fixed gain. These results separate the resources needed to perform a specified quantum operation from those needed for universal state reconstruction. The central connection is operational: physical consistency restricts which distinctions a controller can expose, and the information carried by its complete input determines the cost of doing so. This links a causal requirement to quantitative limits on converting quantum data into computational control.
item.dc:creator: Jeongho Bang, Kyoungho Cho, Jeongwoo Jae

item.title: Coherent Control of Single-Photon Emission in Broadband Plasmonic Resonators
item.description: arXiv:2611.28493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Encoding phase information with quantum emitters in metallic optical nanocavities is challenging due to ultrafast relaxation induced by the broadband nature of the plasmonic near field. Using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory, we demonstrate that an individual emitter strongly coupled to a plasmonic nanocavity field that is driven by a pulsed laser with frequency comb spectrum undergoes spontaneous emission of well-resolved one-photon pulses whose amplitude scales quadratically with the number of frequency comb components due to coherent accumulation, and ultrashort non-exponential temporal profiles with duration set by the light-matter coupling strength. Conditions are discussed for exponentially suppressing the probability of two or more emission events within the lifetime of the coupled emitter-nanocavity system. The spectral signatures of the optimal one-photon wavepackets are discussed. This work paves the way for the development of ultrafast laser-triggered single-photon emitters using atoms and molecules in optical nanocavities.
item.dc:creator: Athul S. Rema, Adri\'an E. Rubio L\'opez, Felipe Herrera

item.title: photon number correlations in harmonics driven with classical and quantum light
item.description: arXiv:2611.28498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent reports of nonclassical intensity correlations in harmonic generation raised questions about whether strong harmonic correlations necessarily imply genuinely quantum behaviour. Here, we compare the low-photon-number perturbative harmonic generation driven by classical and bright squeezed vacuum sources. The latter generates strong auto- and cross-correlations in the harmonic spectrum. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and heralding measurements show that the cross-correlations are fully classical and can be explained by the common fluctuations from the driving field. A visible scaling of the measured correlation function with mean harmonic flux is observed, which is well-explained by a click detector-response model.
item.dc:creator: Katarzyna M. Kowalczyk, Michael T. Weil, Kevin Murzyn, Andr\'e Staudte, Jeff S. Lundeen, David M. Villeneuve, Giulio Vampa

item.title: Subquantum Pilot-Wave System Theory: Structural and Amplitude Nonequilibrium under Source Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.28506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A source in the Schrodinger equation changes the norm of the guiding wave, apparently conflicting with the conservation of probability. In source-extended de Broglie-Bohm dynamics the conflict disappears: probability is carried by the particle ensemble, while the wavefunction guides its motion. The difficulty is then different. What does quantum equilibrium mean when the particle distribution remains normalized but the guiding density does not? We show that the departure has two independent components: a structural one, measured by the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the particle distribution and the normalized guiding density, and an amplitude one, measured by the Born weight. The Born rule holds precisely when both are equilibrated. Their evolution is governed by the complex source-to-wavefunction ratio; scale covariance further distinguishes an independently prescribed source, against which the amplitude of the wave matters, from state-dependent generators for which rescaling remains a symmetry. We develop a source-aware analytical--computational method, combining exact or semi-analytical guiding fields with Bohmian trajectory transport, ensemble quadrature and independent numerical checks. Free-space impulses expose the limits of global diagnostics and an exact jump rule; a driven ring has constant Born weight but either periodic or secular structural departure; oscillators show both source-generated structural change and amplitude-only evolution, including a finite-horizon weak-drive plateau far below its frozen-particle value; and a coupled two-body model exhibits nonlocal guidance and evolving particle entanglement. The source-free, initially equilibrated sector recovers standard quantum mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Said Mikki

item.title: Quantum nonclassicality as a marginal problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.28674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical explanations of quantum statistics---local, noncontextual, or causal---fail for one and the same reason: the probability distributions observed in different contexts are not the marginals of a single joint distribution. Every single context admits a classical model. This is Boole's problem of the "conditions of possible experience." Garg and Mermin treated it as a linear problem and showed, via Farkas's lemma, that its solvability is equivalent to a finite list of Bell-type inequalities, one for each extreme ray of a convex polyhedral cone; Pitowsky gave it the form of correlation polytopes. We sketch this common structure and discuss two examples: Aerts's elastic-band model, which reproduces the quantum cosine in one context but obeys the classical bound when contexts are combined; and nonclassicality in causal data fusion, where the contexts are supplied by interventions on a causal structure.
item.dc:creator: Karl Svozil

item.title: Revealing the Hidden Symmetry of the Asymmetric Quantum Rabi Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.28677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A longitudinal bias breaks ordinary parity in the asymmetric quantum Rabi model, yet exact crossings reappear when the bias equals an integer multiple $m$ of the oscillator energy spacing. We trace the hidden symmetry to exchange between equal-energy partners $m$ rungs apart on two displaced oscillator ladders. Tunneling to other rungs makes this exchange vary in time. We construct the exact symmetry operator by adding spin and oscillator coherences that cancel this variation. At nonzero coupling and tunneling, the resulting charge has no zero modes, and its sign divides the full Hilbert space into two generalized-parity sectors that cannot mix. Spin-resolved mirror interference probes coherence between the two opposite-parity states at a crossing. Its small-displacement exponent gives $m$, and its leading coefficient, together with the charge magnitude, predicts the mixing induced by a slight change in bias.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Min Li, Zi-Cheng Liu, Long-Jie Li, Xuan Zou, Jin-Xiang Fu, Xilin Lu, Murray T. Batchelor

item.title: Phase-dependent atomicity and PPT edge states for cyclic-sign covariant qutrit maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.28700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decomposable positive maps cannot detect entangled states with positive partial transpose (PPT). We obtain a necessary and sufficient criterion for decomposability in the entire seven-real-parameter class of Hermiticity-preserving cyclic-sign covariant maps on $M_3$. The criterion reduces to a one-variable inequality and, for positive maps in this class, characterizes indecomposability exactly. We apply it to a phase-dependent family obtained by adding a completely positive map to the Choi map. Every map in this family is positive, and we find the exact phase-dependent threshold for indecomposability and atomicity. At three phase values, the maps remain indecomposable for every finite deformation strength. Each indecomposable map gives an indecomposable entanglement witness through its Choi matrix. We construct PPT edge states of birank $(5,5)$ detected by these witnesses throughout the indecomposable region.
item.dc:creator: Adam Rutkowski

item.title: Many-Body Flux Selection in Chiral Quantum Batteries
item.description: arXiv:2611.28738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an interacting quantum-battery chain in which a synthetic flux controls interference between hopping paths. Keeping the internal battery Hamiltonian fixed, we seek the flux that leaves the most extractable work. Even a Gaussian reconstruction supplied with exact one-body information can rank competing flux settings incorrectly. A reduced many-body model that retains correlations within a few battery-occupation sectors recovers the correct ranking and selects nearly optimal fluxes across the finite systems and parameter ranges studied. Strikingly, the model can make an accurate control choice even when it excludes configurations carrying substantial probability in the exact state. Thus, choosing a nearly optimal charging flux can require much less information than reconstructing the full many-body state.
item.dc:creator: Borhan Ahmadi

item.title: Sharp Purity Based Entropy Bounds and Machine Learning Assisted Entropy Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.28749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purity quantifies quantum-state mixedness, motivating the study of its role in controlling entropy variations. A sharp purity-based continuity bound is established for the von Neumann entropy of qubit states. The bound is attainable for every admissible purity difference and strictly improves the existing purity bound. In higher dimensions, an explicit sharp bound is derived within the family of pure states mixed with the maximally mixed state. Further continuity estimates are obtained for conditional entropy, quantum mutual information, quantum conditional mutual information, and squashed entanglement within specified bipartite and tripartite families. An application to machine learning assisted qubit entropy estimation illustrates how the sharp bound converts purity estimation errors into rigorous entropy error bounds.
item.dc:creator: Komal Kumar, Shree Prakash

item.title: Quantum Metrology With Quantum Limit Cycles
item.description: arXiv:2611.28801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beyond nonclassical states, emergent quantum phenomena offer new metrological resources. Quantum limit cycles, in particular, sustain long-lived oscillations that prolong coherent signal accumulation. However, quantum fluctuations may limit this advantage, leaving their metrological performance unclear. Here, we propose a quantum limit-cycle metrology protocol for collective spins by introducing nonlinear damping into the conventional collective-decay protocol. We develop a semiclassical phase-diffusion theory to characterize its metrological performance, in good agreement with numerical simulations. The limit-cycle protocol improves estimation precision and approaches Heisenberg scaling with system size. We further combine limit-cycle dynamics with spin squeezing, finding that squeezing improves short-time precision, but phase diffusion ultimately dominates, leaving the asymptotic scaling unchanged. Our results establish quantum limit cycles as a metrological resource and clarify the interplay between limit-cycle dynamics and squeezing in quantum sensing.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Hao Liu, Xiangyu Niu, Keren Li, Ran Liu, Xiao-Dong Yang, Jun Li

item.title: Holevo-Bounded Total Information from Pair Distributions of Alternative Quantum Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.28837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The accessible information of a quantum ensemble can be strictly smaller than its Holevo information because a single-copy measurement may discard part of the label--system correlation. We ask whether information represented across two alternative measurement contexts can bridge this gap without assigning a joint distribution to their outcomes. Building on the relative-entropy-based projection method introduced by Harder et al., we define the directed posterior novelty of each record relative to the other, and an associated total-information quantity. For posterior-orthogonal records, this quantity equals the sum of the two record mutual informations. For finite-dimensional classical--quantum ensembles, we prove that optimizing this quantity over pairs of POVMs yields a value between the accessible and Holevo information. The upper bound follows by showing that the directed posterior novelty provides a lower bound on the infimum of the measured-relative-entropy recovery error. The uniform BB84 ensemble provides an example in which the quantity saturates the Holevo information while strictly exceeding the accessible information. Finally, we analytically establish the quantum validity of a redundancy-based information causality condition, resolving a question that has remained open since the condition was introduced.
item.dc:creator: Baichu Yu, Zhang Zhou, Zhiyuan Li, Jiajun Zhang

item.title: Increasing Quantum LDPC Code Distance through Explicit Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.28847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an explicit construction of quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes without searching for candidates at each size. A fixed pair partition (PP) and fixed integer parameters determine the parity-check matrices at a specified size. Using affine permutation matrices (APMs), we construct a $[[3072,772,32]]$ code with column weight 3 and check weight 8 in each of the X and Z parity-check matrices. A construction based on circulant permutation matrices (CPMs) gives $[[1270,260,\ge34]]$, with column weight 4 and check weight 10. We prove that the construction yields commuting checks and verify the resulting distances using exhaustive search and logical operators. For the main construction, we conjecture the existence of a finite structural distance upper bound and distance improvement toward that bound as the size increases.
item.dc:creator: Kenta Kasai

item.title: The resource--invariant gap: a protected Floquet invariant need not protect Wigner negativity
item.description: arXiv:2611.28904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological invariants constrain a driven Floquet generator, yet whether they protect a transient nonlinear bosonic resource remains open. We track boundary Wigner negativity of an even cat state in a chiral Floquet Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with boundary Kerr nonlinearity and structured loss. The quasienergy windings remain quantized at every chain length, yet the matched sector contrast flips sign when the chain grows under index-end shielding and is null within $3\times 10^{-5}$ under uniform loss at $t=T$ for $d\le 0.5$. Prepared and shielded on the physical dangling end, the contrast remains positive, modulated by local dimer return rather than set by the invariant. A three-site causal light cone and a boundary-Laplacian erosion law trace the flip to strong-bond bulk exposure: the sign is set by where the bulk-rate loss sits relative to the prepared site, not by chain length. We call this decoupling the resource--invariant gap.
item.dc:creator: Juste Deuyekbe, Philippe Djorw\'e, Nsangou Mama, S. G. Nana Engo

item.title: Long-time dynamics of open quantum systems: mathematical and physical aspects
item.description: arXiv:2611.28906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum channels provide the mathematical framework for describing the evolution of open quantum systems, i.e., quantum systems interacting with an environment. This review focuses on the long-time or asymptotic dynamics of open quantum systems, a topic of growing interest due to its relevance for quantum information theory and noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. We present a comprehensive analysis of homogeneous evolutions in both discrete and continuous time, treating the dynamics in full generality within the Schr\"odinger and Heisenberg pictures. By systematically studying the spectral properties of quantum channels, we present general structure theorems that characterize asymptotic behaviour, illustrated through several paradigmatic examples. We further discuss how the asymptotic dynamics can be exploited for dissipative state engineering, the identification of decoherence-free subspaces, the design of quantum error-correction schemes, and the evaluation of the asymptotic capacities of quantum channels.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Amato, Paolo Facchi, Giovanni Gramegna, Arturo Konderak

item.title: Non-Abelian Twist Defects in Bivariate Bicycle Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.28944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity-check codes combine efficient quantum storage with a rich Abelian anyon structure, providing a compelling platform for exploring the interplay between quantum error correction and topological order. A central challenge is how to realize domain walls that host non-Abelian twist defects at their endpoints. Here we explicitly construct electric-magnetic duality walls for arbitrary bivariate bicycle codes with finite anyon content using composite, interblock, and patch checks. These checks remove the unwanted local modes while preserving charge conversion, ensuring that topologically contractible closed ribbons act trivially on encoded states. For each fixed code, check weights and interaction ranges remain bounded independently of wall length. The wall endpoints have quantum dimension $2^{Q/2}$, where $Q$ counts the independent generators in each electric or magnetic charge space. As an application, we illustrate measurement-only braiding for $Q=3$ under the correspondence between measurements and defect transport. Our construction provides a valuable basis for exploring non-Abelian defect physics and developing logical operations in quantum low-density parity-check codes with Abelian topological order in future.
item.dc:creator: Rui Zeng, Li-Wei Yu

item.title: Q-TRACE: Physics-based zero-day attack detection for decoy-state quantum key distribution
item.description: arXiv:2611.28945v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Practical quantum key distribution (QKD) is secure only while its devices match the assumptions of the security proof, and implementation attacks exploit mismatches while keeping the quantum bit error rate (QBER) low. We formulate attack detection in decoy-state BB84 as a sequential test against the honest-device manifold, the set of receiver statistics an attack-free link can produce under arbitrary channel loss. The resulting monitor, Q-TRACE (Quantum Telemetry Residuals Against Calibrated Expectations), calibrates a physical model of each link on commissioning data, profiles out the transmittance, and combines omnibus residual, physics score and setting-allocation tests with drift-robust references; no attack data are used. The formulation also yields a detectability exponent D* that lower-bounds the delay of any telemetry monitor and vanishes for a Trojan-horse probe with filtered back-reflection. On a count-level twin with model mismatch, over five held-out seeds and at a per-window false-alarm rate of 10^-3, Q-TRACE detects 63.6% of links under known attacks, 28.0% under unseen attack families and 65.3% under composite attacks, versus at most 51.2%, 6.7% and 42.3% for industry monitors, unsupervised and quantum-kernel detectors and a supervised classifier. Its delay attains the bound for strongly detectable attacks. On 33 parallel BB84 links of the IBM Heron processor ibm_marrakesh with physically executed entangling and amplitude-damping eavesdroppers, the measured information-disturbance relations agree with theory; a commissioning reference acquired under different operating conditions triggers alarms in every monitor tested, while a condition-matched reference detects a probe with 0.3% ideal QBER increase on 14 of 14 link-epochs with no false alarm on 66 honest ones.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Tapas Chongder (Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur, Jodhpur, India)

item.title: On locked states for damped driven Jaynes--Cummings equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.28962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider damped driven version of the Jaynes-Cummings equation which describes quantised one-mode Maxwell field coupled to a two-level molecule. The pumping and dissipation operator are polynomial in the creation and annihilation operators. The structure of the dissipation operator corresponds to the theory of completely positive trace preserving operators due to Lindblad, Kossakowski and others. We construct examples of {\it locked states} which are stationary states of the corresponding averaged dynamics in the interaction picture. The states are nonnegative Hermitian density operators with finite Hilbert-Schmidt norm. The calculations rely on the recurrence equation for diagonal entries.
item.dc:creator: A. I. Komech, E. A. Kopylova

item.title: Perfect state transfer on trees in the normalized Laplacian quantum walk
item.description: arXiv:2611.28984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, in the normalized-Laplacian model, perfect state transfer between two vertices of a tree can only happen if they are at distance at most $2$. We show that a conjecture of Coutinho and Baptista, stating that the only trees admitting perfect state transfer are $K_2$ and $P_3$, is true when the two vertices are at odd distance. We then construct infinite families of trees admitting perfect state transfer, disproving their conjecture in the general case.
item.dc:creator: Laureline Polli

item.title: A Frequency-Learning Interpolation-Based Coordinate Descent Method to Optimize Parameterized Quantum Circuits on Quantum Hardware
item.description: arXiv:2611.29019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structure-aware optimizers have been the focus of recent study for the optimization of parameters in variational quantum circuits. Many of these optimizers follow a coordinate-based paradigm, making single parameter updates by using classical approximations to the cost function generated from quantum sampling. However, the performance of structure-aware optimizers on real quantum hardware at large system size has yet to be demonstrated. Recently, Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (ICD) has been proposed to unify many of these optimizers into one framework. ICD requires a preset frequency set for interpolation, which can be theoretically derived, but for which the cost function is generally sparse over and may require manual tuning. To address these issues, we propose Frequency-learning Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (FLICD) to adaptively learn frequencies online, allowing easier scaling up to larger systems. We demonstrate that our algorithm is more accurate than an existing zeroth-order method COBYLA and requires fewer quantum resources than ICD on simulator. Using IBM quantum hardware, we execute FLICD on systems up to 100 qubits and observe robust performance with an increasing number of layers.
item.dc:creator: Jack Mandell (Department of Mathematical Sciences, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Adam Leicester (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Zixu Wang (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Jian Shi (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, Department of Physics, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute), Haimeng Zhang (IBM Quantum, IBM T.J. Watson Research Center), Yangyang Xu (Department of Mathematical Sciences, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute)

item.title: Compact and Long-Term Stable Polarization Entangled Photon-Pair Source
item.description: arXiv:2611.29046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a robust, compact polarization-entangled photon-pair source based on bulk optics that achieves long-term stability, a spectral pair generation rate of $4.24 \times 10^6$ pairs s$^{-1}$ mW$^{-1}$ nm$^{-1}$ constant for pump powers up to 700 mW, an intrinsic heralding efficiency of 59.8% , and a polarization contrast visibility of 99.6%. The source is mechanically designed for vibrational robustness, employing an engineered base plate and a reduced optical layout for less alignment sensitivity and complexity. It operates at telecom wavelengths in C-band with a typical type-0 SPDC spectral output of 70 nm width. We demonstrate its integration into a deployed entanglement-based QKD system that bridges the gap between laboratory prototypes and practical quantum communication hardware.
item.dc:creator: Mirela Selimovi\'{c}, Josip Bajo, Mikl\'{o}s Horv\'{a}th, Juan Jos\'e Romero, Thomas Heine, Philip Walther, Rupert Ursin, Sebastian Philipp Neumann

item.title: Single-Phonon-Gated Pair Charging of Quantum Batteries
item.description: arXiv:2611.29130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charging a quantum battery requires both an energy source and access to a channel through which that energy can be transferred. If that access depends on a quantum state, charging becomes conditional on the state while the external controls remain unchanged. We show that a single phonon in a common mechanical mode enables a second-order resonant pair transition in a two-cell battery formed by the electronic spins of two nitrogen-vacancy centers, whereas the mechanical vacuum supports no corresponding resonance. At fixed controls and mean phonon number, the final stored energy and ergotropy reached with a one-phonon Fock state are unattainable with any classical mixture of coherent states. An energy balance shows that the microwave drives supply nearly all of the stored energy, while the phonon contributes only a small fraction. Our results open a route to quantum-state-conditioned charging in quantum batteries under experimentally feasible parameters.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolong Zhao, Yazhuang Miao, Shuo Liang, Tianhui Qiu, Libin Fu

item.title: Undecidable quantum storage: no algorithm can tell from the noise rate whether a fixed circuit remembers
item.description: arXiv:2611.29134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Below a threshold noise rate, error correction lets larger quantum memories store a qubit for longer, without limit. Can the noise rate alone tell us whether a given noisy circuit does this? We construct fixed local circuits for which no algorithm can, already in one dimension under single-qubit noise. Each circuit is translation-invariant and time-periodic, with depolarizing noise on every wire after every layer, including all classical control. A computable list of disjoint rate intervals is indexed by the inputs $n$ of a universal Turing machine; local noise statistics select the input that the circuit simulates, and halting triggers erasure. If the machine runs forever on $n$, a qubit is stored throughout the $n$-th interval at entanglement fidelity at least $15/16$ for a time that grows without bound with size: linearly on rings, exponentially in six dimensions. The encoding and decoding maps are noiseless and global; they depend on $n$, the system size and, for decoding, the time, but not on the rate. If it halts, the fidelity of every encoding falls below $1/2+\eta$, for any fixed $\eta>0$, after a time independent of size and rate. The labels of the intervals with unbounded storage form a $\Pi^0_1$-complete set, and intervals of both kinds accumulate at zero, so these circuits have no noise threshold. Without rate selection, the ring construction is a translation-invariant, time-periodic memory: from an initialized classical hierarchy it stores a qubit for a time linear in the ring length at every sufficiently small rate, addressing the memory part of a one-dimensional question raised by D\"unnweber, Styliaris and Trivedi. These are existence results: registers and interaction ranges are very large and the rates astronomically small.
item.dc:creator: Seth Douglas, Nidhal Mghirbi

item.title: Where to Hide the Traps: Robust Placement in Verifiable Blind Quantum Computation
item.description: arXiv:2611.29258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trap-based verification of blind quantum computation hides test qubits among the positions of a measurement pattern, and existing protocols choose the trap configuration without regard to the delegated computation. We model trap placement as a zero-sum game between a client, who chooses a trap distribution, and a server, who chooses where to apply a Pauli deviation, with a damage profile $w$ and a per-trap detection constant $c$. Since the client cannot know how damage from several positions combines, we solve the game for all monotone subadditive damage functions consistent with $w$ at once. In a single round, placing traps in proportion to $w$ guarantees soundness error $1-c/\|w\|_1$ and is optimal up to a factor $1+\max_iw_i$, while the optimistic solution can fail completely. Over $T$ test rounds, the error decays exponentially against a server that repeats the same deviation, but a general server can keep it at $\Theta(\|w\|_1/(cT))$, and against such servers the damage-weighted placement is exactly optimal. Damage profiles follow from the flow of the pattern: for brickwork patterns with $m=4h+1$ columns, only $(2h+1)^2$ positions can affect a decision qubit, whatever the width. With $k$ traps per round, placing them on this set reduces the number of test rounds by the same factor as for a single trap; with unrestricted trap sets and flat damage we recover the known optimality of fractional coloring. Finally, trap statistics certify the aggregate damage with a number of rounds independent of the number of positions $N$, whereas locating the damage requires $\Omega(N\epsilon^{-2}\log\delta^{-1})$ rounds.
item.dc:creator: Noureldin Mohamed, Saif Al-Kuwari

item.title: Quantum Geometric Tensor in Parameter-Dependent Quasi-Hermitian Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.29314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A parameter-dependent physical inner product makes the comparison of quantum states at different parameter points non-unique. We formulate two geometric prescriptions for this comparison in quasi-Hermitian systems. The Type I QGT is defined by an inner-product-compatible covariant derivative and horizontal projection. It is a Hermitian, positive-semidefinite Gram tensor, and, for any normalized solution of the inner-product-preserving dynamics, its tangential component equals the physical energy variance. The Type II QGT is constructed from the endpoint overlap of physical dual states and is invariant under local $GL(1,\mathbb{C})$ rescalings. We show that, on a normalized section, it coincides with the established left--right (LR) QGT, while providing an endpoint-overlap interpretation of that tensor. Our central result is an exact relation between the two constructions: in the positive Dyson frame, the Type I QGT is the positive Gram block of the dressed-derivative sector, while the real symmetric part of the Type II QGT is this metric minus a positive-semidefinite contribution from the metric connection; the full complex tensor also contains cross terms. This relation clarifies the origin of the possible indefiniteness of the Type II metric and separates it from the positivity of the physical Hilbert-space metric. We further distinguish instantaneous Dyson mappings from the fixed inner-product-preserving dynamics and characterize the conditions under which the corresponding QGTs agree. Three two-level models illustrate these results. The physical content of the two tensors is then identified through the energy uncertainty and evolution speed for Type I, and the symmetrized endpoint overlap, complex holonomy, and signed dynamical response for Type II.
item.dc:creator: Ming-Zhang Wang, Xu-Yang Hou, Hao Guo

item.title: Approximation of Semigroups of Random Processes on a Hilbert Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.29359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops Chernoff-type approximation methods for strongly continuous and bi-continuous semigroups of operators arising in the stochastic dynamics of quantum systems. The main focus is on applying Chernoff iterations to Markov semigroups of multiplicative random processes on separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The justification of the passage from discrete quantum measurements to continuous ones depends essentially on the choice of topology and function spaces. We propose conditions for convergence to bi-continuous semigroups on subspaces that weaken the classical requirements of the Chernoff theorem. The existence of the limiting bi-continuous semigroup is established in each of the three cases: commutation of the approximating operators, their asymptotic commutation, and uniform convergence of difference quotients over a family of approximating operators. For diffusive models with a generator having bounded coefficients, the derivative of the approximating function is computed explicitly on the subspace of test functions with rapidly decreasing second derivative; the limitations of applicability of this result are discussed. Applications to generalized models of continuous imprecise quantum measurement with unbounded observables, as well as to Poisson and diffusion processes, are outlined as directions for further research.
item.dc:creator: A. V. Utkin

item.title: Optimizer or physics? Machine-learning surrogates for collision-based preparation of multipartite entangled quantum states
item.description: arXiv:2611.29384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeated partial-SWAP collisions can prepare symmetric Dicke states, including the $W$ state, without measurement or postselection. The collision sequence uses only two global collision angles, and its fidelity is evaluated after a final layer of local phase rotations is optimized numerically, so each candidate pair requires a many-qubit simulation and a phase fit. We study when learned surrogates reduce the number of such evaluations, and what limits the best-found fidelity, for 65 Dicke targets with 11--20 qubits in noiseless simulations. At 50 evaluations per target, Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization (GP-BO) exceeds fixed Sobol and grid designs by 0.088 and 0.063 in mean best-found fidelity. Bounded Nelder--Mead reaches 0.760 against 0.762 for GP-BO, and has the higher three-seed mean on 41 of the 61 targets with a reference value; in this two-parameter problem, adaptivity matters far more than the choice between the two methods. A neural-network ensemble pretrained on 750 observations from smaller systems needs 32\% fewer new evaluations per target than GP-BO at comparable fidelity, but the full neural search takes 1.6 times the wall time of GP-BO in our implementation. In a separate source-only test, the best of five neural proposals per target exceeds the best of five population-model proposals by 0.070 in mean fidelity. Exact symmetries and state diagnostics help explain why the leading adaptive methods reach similar family-mean fidelities. The collisions conserve the magnitude of the bare Dicke overlap and the total-spin weights, and for the best controls on a 12-target diagnostic panel, 79% of the infidelity is an amplitude deficit that a final phase layer cannot remove, which motivates interleaved phase control.
item.dc:creator: Duc-Kha Vu, Minh Tam Nguyen, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustacapl{\i}o\u{g}lu, Fatih Ozaydin

item.title: Bogoliubov-picture thermofield dynamics in anharmonic environments
item.description: arXiv:2611.29427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermofield dynamics (TFD) describes finite-temperature quantum relaxation through a purified wavefunction, without sampling thermally populated initial states. For harmonic environments, TFD is typically combined with a thermal Bogoliubov transformation to obtain a compact wavefunction representation. This transformation can also be useful for anharmonic baths, but preparing the corresponding thermal state in the transformed representation poses additional numerical challenges. Here, we explore TFD approaches tailored to anharmonic potentials and compatible with efficient tensor network methods for quantum propagation. We show that the conceptually appealing route of converting a harmonic-reference thermal state into the target anharmonic state by imaginary-time propagation can be numerically ill-conditioned. As a practical alternative, we formulate a multilayer multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree (ML-MCTDH) protocol that separates thermal-state preparation from the harmonic-reference Bogoliubov transformation. We prepare the thermal purification in the bare representation and then apply finite-basis Bogoliubov unitaries to the physical--auxiliary mode pairs. For independent bath modes, direct construction of the thermal amplitude provides a complementary initialization procedure. We illustrate this protocol through vibrational relaxation and spatial-superposition decoherence of a harmonic subsystem coupled to a Morse-oscillator bath. We find non-monotonic energy relaxation, shifts in the dominant resonant response, and oscillatory energy exchange at zero and finite temperature. For decoherence, we recover the expected harmonic-bath scaling and find a pronounced non-monotonic dependence of the decay rate on anharmonicity at finite temperature in a low-frequency model, with a weaker dependence in a high-frequency model.
item.dc:creator: Rocco Martinazzo, Bartosz B{\l}asiak, Irene Burghardt

item.title: No-Go Theorems for Transversal and Automorphism Clifford Gates on Prime-Dimensional Qudit Stabilizer Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.29430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Logical Clifford gates are a basic primitive of fault-tolerant quantum computation. For stabilizer codes on qudits of prime dimension $p$ that encode $k\geq 2$ logical qudits, we prove that Clifford gadgets that are transversal with respect to a fixed partition of the physical qudits into blocks of fewer than $k$ qudits cannot realize the full logical Clifford group, and that this block size is tight. Code automorphisms, which combine single-qudit Clifford gates with qudit permutations, also fail for every $p$. Both obstructions come from prime-order logical Clifford elements that these gadgets cannot reach.
item.dc:creator: Yuchen Zhan, Qi Ye, Dong-Ling Deng

item.title: Multi-port few-photon diodes
item.description: arXiv:2611.29451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate single- and two-photon scattering dynamics in a system comprising two one dimensional chiral waveguides coupled to a dissipative Rydberg atom pair. By employing the Laplace transform method, we analytically solve the scattering problem and characterize the transport properties. Our results demonstrate robust perfect single-photon diode effects in this system with or without dissipation, exhibiting unity transmittance in the forward direction and zero transmittance in the backward direction. Unlike previous studies where perfect nonreciprocity requires a specific dissipation rate, our scheme achieves this effect without fine-tuning such parameters. Furthermore, we extend the nonreciprocal transport to multi-port configurations at the one and two-photon levels. The system exhibits pronounced photon nonreciprocal behavior in lossy and lossless scenarios, without the need for precise parameter matching. This work provides a robust platform for on-chip nonreciprocal photonic devices.
item.dc:creator: Teng-Fei Xiao, Liang Li, Renli Xu, Tiantian Li, Junlong Tian, Jinlei Tan, Jie Peng

item.title: Scaling of phase rigidity without eigenstate coalescence
item.description: arXiv:2611.29463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase rigidity vanishes as a power law near exceptional points, reflecting the coalescence of eigenstates at these points. In this Letter, we show that non-Hermitian skin effects induce distinct asymptotic behaviors of phase rigidity without eigenstate coalescence. To demonstrate this, we derive exact analytical results for three non-Hermitian chain models and verify them numerically. For the ordinary skin effect, phase rigidity decays exponentially with increasing system size $N$, as the right and left eigenstates are exponentially localized at opposite boundaries. For the scale-free skin effect, phase rigidity exhibits an $N^{-2}$ power-law approach to a nonzero constant as the right and left eigenstates have decay lengths proportional to $N$. For the algebraic skin effect studied here, phase rigidity can exhibit an $N^{-1/2}$ power-law decay to zero, with the right eigenstate algebraically localized near a boundary and the left eigenstate spread across the chain. These findings show that non-Hermitian skin effects govern phase-rigidity scaling by shaping the spatial profiles of the right and left eigenstates, enabling control of eigenstate nonorthogonality without exceptional points.
item.dc:creator: Shang-En Xie, Li-Mei Chen, Yao Zhou, Peng Ye

item.title: A single-photon quantum sensor via single-atom cavity-QED
item.description: arXiv:2611.29464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a cavity-QED sensor using an optical probe with exactly one photon per pulse. This has a better sensitivity than a coherent pulse with the same average power when no global coherent phase reference is available. The sensor measurement is based on the estimation of the Raman-controlled absorption probability of a single-photon pulse. We use the Fock state master equation to determine the dynamics and performance of the Raman-controlled absorption of a single photon pulse and optimise the sensitivity using machine learning. Two examples are presented; (1) the target parameter is the detuning of the two-level system itself, and (2) the target parameters describe a remote reflecting cavity. In the second case, the scheme does not require a shared coherent phase reference.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Burns, Mattias Keller, G J Milburn

item.title: Unveiling the Action of Randomized Compiling on Quantum States: A Geometric Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2611.29488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Randomized compiling (RC) converts coherent errors into stochastic Pauli noise, but this conversion alone does not imply isotropic contraction of the output state. Here we use the generalized Bloch vector (GBV) representation to examine the cumulative effect of RC on state purity and orientation in multi-layer circuits. For the independent, isotropically distributed weak coherent errors considered here, the accumulated ensemble-averaged RC channel lies close to the depolarizing direction, producing a state-level near-isotropic contraction that sacrifices a small amount of purity to achieve a substantial suppression of orientational deviation. When dephasing coexists, RC suppresses the coherent-error contribution but leaves a residual deviation dominated by dephasing, setting a limit that we term the "dephasing wall". We experimentally validate these findings on a superconducting quantum processor through GHZ state preparation and phase estimation in a simulation of topological braiding. The results confirm that RC's effectiveness stems from its ability to suppress the orientational bias of coherent errors---a structural transformation not resolved by fidelity alone but directly visible through GBV diagnostics.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tang, Chao Zhan, Yao Song, Peiling Huang, Yuxuan Zhou, Song Liu, Junkai Zeng, Jiansheng Wu, Tongxing Yan, Xiu-Hao Deng, Yuanzhen Chen

item.title: Interaction-Driven Photocurrent Enhancement in a Quantum Photocell with Opposite Transient and Steady-State Responses
item.description: arXiv:2611.29516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study photocurrent control in a quantum photocell with interacting qubit-qutrit donors coupled to an acceptor. We show that stronger Heisenberg exchange coupling and anisotropy increase the transient photocurrent but reduce its steady-state value, whereas the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction favors steady-state output at the expense of transient enhancement. This reversal highlights the need to distinguish rapid current generation from sustained operation when tuning quantum photovoltaic devices. Analysis of donor purity further reveals that the qutrit's local purity tracks the photocurrent trends in both regimes. These results demonstrate that the effects of donor interactions depend crucially on the timescale of operation, suggesting a strategy for tailoring the response of hybrid quantum photocells to different operating regimes.
item.dc:creator: Abbas Shokri, Esfandyar Faizi, Mohammad B. Arjmandi

item.title: On-demand frequency-entangled microwave biphotons from a transmon-resonator dimer
item.description: arXiv:2611.29529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a superconducting circuit QED source of on-demand frequency-entangled microwave photon pairs, with one photon emitted into each of two separate waveguides, enabling individual manipulation. The design is based on a transmon-resonator dimer, which consists of two transmon-resonator subsystems coupled through a cross-Kerr interaction. We outline a viable circuit-QED realization in which the required cross-Kerr interaction is implemented using Josephson-junction couplers. To analyze the emission dynamics, we derive and numerically solve the set of evolution equations that enable tracking the evolution of the joint spectral intensity of photons. We characterize the resulting photon-number correlations, frequency anticorrelation, and spectral entanglement. By varying the coupling strengths, we obtain biphotons with distinct joint spectral intensities and Schmidt spectra, ranging from broadly distributed multimode entanglement to states dominated by two nearly equally weighted Schmidt contributions. In the latter regime, optimizing the transmon-resonator coupling and detuning yields an output biphoton state that has fidelity $F \approx 0.956$ with a two-dimensional maximally entangled state. Restricting the local target modes to separated frequency bins yields a fidelity $F_\mathrm{bin} \approx 0.949$, indicating that the output state closely approximates a frequency-bin Bell pair. Thus, the proposed microwave biphoton source provides a route toward distributing frequency-encoded quantum resources between remote superconducting nodes.
item.dc:creator: E. V. Stolyarov, O. V. Kliushnichenko

item.title: Differentiable collision-model control for multipartite state engineering: reachability, geometry, and preparation cost
item.description: arXiv:2611.29556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a differentiable control architecture for multipartite state engineering in which partial-SWAP collisions, a Heisenberg exchange, are interleaved with layers of local phase rotations. Singular collision angles confine the evolution to invariant supports, impose exact fidelity ceilings, and generate an inverse-distance lower bound on the preparation time nearby. Away from them, numerical certificates show that the sampled couplings reach the whole fixed-excitation sector for sector dimensions up to 21, and optimizations reach fidelities above 0.999 for dimensions up to 1716. At generic couplings the number of rounds needed for a given Dicke fidelity, measured by the ratio of independent phase controls to the projective dimension, is nearly independent of the system size, and the quantum Fisher information spectrum is close to that of a random Gaussian Jacobian. Near full SWAP, a slow-time theory, the sharp form of the inverse-distance bound there, predicts microscopic hitting times without fitted parameters: the distance from the singular point sets the clock and its direction selects the effective control geometry. A detuning sweep along two rays shows that the Dicke horizon follows this law up to a detuning of 0.1, where it is two to five times shorter than at a generic coupling in sectors of dimension 70 to 252, while phase-uniform, random-sign, and Haar-random targets are delayed; beyond a detuning of about 0.3 all targets return to the generic cost. The slow-time value for the Dicke target is nearly the same for sector dimensions from 35 to 252. The exchange graph of the effective theory offers an interpretation of this ordering. Counted in two-qubit gates, generic-coupling preparation is costlier than known Dicke circuits; the architecture offers fixed global couplings, local phase rotations as the only control, and no measurement.
item.dc:creator: Minh Tam Nguyen, Duc-Kha Vu, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu, Fatih Ozaydin

item.title: Non unitary and nonlinear quantum generative large model design and fast large-scale training without back propagation
item.description: arXiv:2611.29571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformer-based large models require huge computational and storage costs. Quantum computation is expected to address that due to its potential to speed up classical algorithms exponentially. Key challenges of implementing quantum large models include the linear, unitary nature of qubit evolutions contrast with the non-unitary matrices and nonlinear functions in classical Transformers, as well as the difficulty of implementing gradient back-propagation on quantum hardware. Here we propose a fully quantum large model containing all the Transformer layers, implementing the non-unitary transformations through SVD-decomposition-based quantum circuits, and approximated nonlinear activation functions through pre-trained parameterized quantum circuits. We also propose a quantum circuit training algorithm based on multi-agent Reinforcement Learning, which can train large-scale parameterized quantum circuits without back-propagation. The dependency between the inference time complexity and the model's hidden dimension has been reduced from polynomial to logarithmic, showing an exponential advantage. The inference executions on the quantum hardware verify our model's 300-1000 times speed-up, and the measurements on the sequence-to-sequence tasks shows its learning ability. The training algorithm achieves only 25% complexity of the best SOTA quantum circuit training algorithms, especially this ratio decreases fast as the parameter scale increases. Our work not only proposes a quantum large model that can significantly reduce the computational cost, but also promotes the quantum computation towards general computing.
item.dc:creator: Tianze Zhu, Xiaofeng Jiang, Min Liao, Luying Zhang, Ruixi Liu, Sen Kuang, Yongzhe Lin, Chenhao Zhou, Shuangwu Chen, Huasen He, Xiaobin Tan, Quan Zheng, Jian Yang

item.title: Feed-Forward Dimension Control for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution over Time-Varying Airborne Free-Space Links
item.description: arXiv:2611.29583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-dimensional quantum key distribution tolerates more noise than qubit-based protocols, but the dimension that maximizes the secret key depends on turbulence, background light, device imperfections, and block size, all of which change during an airborne or satellite pass. Finite-size security analyses of high-dimensional protocols fix the dimension in advance, and the dimension-adaptive schemes reported so far have been analyzed only asymptotically. Here, a controller sets the dimension, acceptance thresholds, and key length of each block using only public data from earlier blocks. Each block is therefore a standard fixed-length protocol, and composable finite-key security against coherent attacks follows from sequential composition; an inaccurate channel model reduces the key rate but does not weaken security. The controller estimates turbulence from observed error rates, maximizes the expected key under forecast uncertainty, and recalibrates its model online. We evaluate it on a simulated entanglement-based orbital-angular-momentum link between an aircraft and a ground station, using Kolmogorov phase screens and the Hufnagel--Valley turbulence profile. Accounting for forecast uncertainty increases the key by 31\%--47\% relative to a naive planner. Over night, dawn, daytime, and model-mismatch scenarios, the recalibrated controller retains at least 98.8\% of the key obtained with the best fixed dimension for each scenario, while every fixed dimension drops to 73.5\% or less in at least one scenario. Running the link's measurement statistics on a superconducting quantum processor shows device errors close to a constant offset; with these errors included, the best daytime dimension changes from eight to four, and the controller adjusts accordingly.
item.dc:creator: Murtuza Lemonwala, Laxima Niure Kandel

item.title: Just another Markovian embedding for open quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.29605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, I present one more method for analysis of non-Markovian open quantum systems by embedding them into larger Markovian systems. As many other approaches, this method starts from finding a rational approximation for the bath correlation function in the frequency domain, the difference is that I retain $\omega \to -\overline \omega$ symmetry for the poles of the approximation. This allows to reduce the dimension of embedding from one- to half-degree-of-freedom per pole. In case of odd number of poles, the resulting equation describing dynamics of the system turns out to be not a Lindblad, but a hybrid quantum-classical master equation.
item.dc:creator: Vasilii Vadimov

item.title: Network contextuality beyond binary outcomes
item.description: arXiv:2611.29626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can a joint measurement reveal nonclassical behaviour in independently prepared systems that share no entanglement? We study network contextuality by extending the two-qubit test of bi-contextuality [G. Ruffolo et al., arXiv:2507.08461 (2025)] to projective measurements with more than two outcomes. In one laboratory, an observer measures the systems individually or jointly performs two compatible global measurements constructed from them. The individual probabilities constrain the possible classical correlations at each source. For our preparations, every noncontextual model with outcome-deterministic and source-independent assignments predicts a nonzero average product of the two global outcomes. The joint quantum measurement gives zero. We construct explicit product states realizing this contradiction for $N=d$ independent sources, each preparing one $d$-dimensional system, with $2\leq d\leq9$. We derive an inequality in observed probabilities, prove its single-source bounds are exact for these preparations, and give sufficient thresholds for violations under independent depolarizing noise. For this family of preparations the dimension range is sharp: for every $d\geq10$ the individual probabilities admit a zero assigned average, so the certificate fails. The same data admit a noncontextual explanation when source independence is relaxed.
item.dc:creator: Hao Zhang, Gerard John Wong Zhongwei, Rafael Rabelo, Gabriel Ruffolo, Pawe{\l} Kurzy\'nski, Dagomir Kaszlikowski

item.title: Direct quantum simulation of compressible Navier-Stokes flow via finite homotopy linearisation
item.description: arXiv:2611.29631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a direct quantum simulation algorithm for finite homotopy approximations to the non-isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes equations. A primitive-variable formulation gives polynomial residuals in the fields and their spatial and time derivatives, including density-weighted time derivatives. On a periodic grid, applying each spatial stencil uniformly to every factor in a shifted product preserves the dynamics of the finite homotopy hierarchy in an affine linearisation. Because each deformation equation depends only on lower homotopy orders, the lifted generator matrix is strictly block lower-triangular and hence nilpotent. The resulting finite-polynomial solution evaluates the final state directly without time-stepping error, while explicit short-time convergence conditions bound the homotopy truncation error on a fixed grid. In two-dimensional Taylor-Green flow, initial pressure balance removes the leading longitudinal acceleration and delays the onset of dilatational kinetic energy from quadratic to quartic in time. At Mach numbers 0.2 and 0.4, the fifth-order hierarchy reproduces viscous dissipation over a longer interval than pressure-dilatation at the same relative tolerance. We identify auxiliary variables representing the same evolving product, compile the finite-polynomial evolution into logical quantum circuits, and recover a signed velocity Fourier mode via Hadamard interference. Together, the Taylor-Green energy budgets quantify the accuracy windows of each homotopy order, while coarse-grid circuits verify the signed readout and measure gate counts. For higher-order evolution on finer grids, merging coincident stencil terms and combining block-encoded products along strictly increasing homotopy-order paths substantially reduce the predicted normalisation cost.
item.dc:creator: Ming-Yang Tan, Guo-Ping Guo, Zhao-Yun Chen

item.title: Quantum tomography of ququart states of optical vector vortices based on measurements in mutually unbiased bases
item.description: arXiv:2611.29633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we present an original method for quantum state tomography of vector optical vortices with an axially symmetric transverse polarization profile. We present an interference technique which allows one to distinguish states of vector vortices with a fixed topological charge with high accuracy. We also demonstrate the feasibility of experimental quantum tomography of the density matrix in the logical ququart space built on vector vortices, with high fidelity for all 20 basis states. It is shown that the proposed tomography scheme provides a uniform characterization of states in all mutually unbiased bases of the ququart space.
item.dc:creator: D. D. Reshetnikov, E. V. Maliutina, T. K. Korol, E. A. Vashukevich, T. Yu. Golubeva

item.title: Extraction erases the gain: cavity loss bounds dynamical-Casimir metrology at ultrastrong coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.29634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultrastrong light--matter coupling dresses the vacuum with virtual photons whose response to the coupling strength exceeds that of any coherent probe, yet these photons never leave the cavity and cannot be detected. A parametric drive at the dynamical-Casimir resonance converts them into real photons that a detector can collect. We show that this conversion is self-limiting: converting the virtual photons of an ultrastrongly coupled probe into real, extractable photons opens the cavity port that removes them, so the retained metrological gain is set by the accumulated cavity loss rather than by the pure-state ceiling. In the driven quantum Rabi model the pure-state quantum Fisher information on the coupling reaches $1.7\times10^{5}$ times the coherent baseline; at a cavity linewidth of $246$~MHz, typical of coplanar-waveguide flux-qubit circuits, master-equation dynamics retain $0.96\%$ of it. In a 32-qubit Dicke model the retained fraction is $2.6\%$ at the largest photon basis computed. Eighteen lossy configurations from both models fall on one curve of the accumulated loss, the product of linewidth and interrogation time, which halves the retained information at $0.13$. The extraction cost, not the lossless ceiling, is the figure of merit for any protocol that reads bound vacuum correlations through a lossy port.
item.dc:creator: Juste Deuyekbe, Philippe Djorw\'e, Nsangou Mama, Serge Guy Nana Engo

item.title: Controlled Continuous-Time Quantum Walks for Power Grid Analysis under N-x Contingencies
item.description: arXiv:2611.29648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The combinatorial growth of network configurations under N-x contingencies presents significant computational challenges for power system analysis. In this work, we introduce a quantum algorithm based on Controlled Continuous-Time Quantum Walks (CCTQWs) that evolves a quantum walker conditioned on a contingency register held in a uniform superposition of all x-line outage configurations representing the contingency scenarios. The proposed framework encodes transmission line availability in a quantum register and employs controlled Hamiltonian evolution to account for topology changes induced by contingencies. We develop a gate-based implementation using Trotter-Suzuki product formulas and investigate the associated approximation errors and computational requirements. As a demonstration of the proposed methodology, we introduce a contingency-averaged occupation centrality measure derived from quantum-walk measurement statistics. Numerical experiments on an 8-bus power network under N-2 contingencies demonstrate the implementation of the algorithm and characterize the convergence of the resulting centrality estimates with respect to the observation window, sampling and Trotter steps. Comparison with established classical centrality measures shows a qualitatively consistent characterization of network structure, particularly in identifying the most central nodes. The proposed framework establishes a methodological foundation for quantum-walk-based analysis of power networks under contingencies, providing a starting point for future investigations of quantum algorithms for power system security assessment.
item.dc:creator: Mahesh N. Jayakody, Ruben Kara, Carsten Hartmann, Andrea Benigni

item.title: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.29650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an improved upper bound on the two-way-assisted capacities of the qubit amplitude-damping channel with decay probability $\gamma$, given by $\log_2[1+(1-\gamma)\gamma^{\gamma/(1-\gamma)}]$. It applies to quantum communication, entanglement distribution, private communication, and secret-key agreement, and, for every $0<\gamma<1$, strictly improves the PLOB relative-entropy bound, the analytic max-relative-entropy bound, and the optimized balanced squashed-entanglement bound. At high damping, a known triple-rail protocol attains more than $99.54\%$ of its leading coefficient. Our method extends sector teleportation simulation to qubits: phase rotations and permutations give exact simulations within fixed-excitation subspaces while preserving the two-level input structure. We determine the exact, additive relative entropy of entanglement of the amplitude-damping resources and the exact regularized entanglement gain at fixed input population. We then derive explicit bounds for generalized amplitude damping, which includes thermal excitation. Combining the amplitude-damping gain with unital and entanglement-breaking channels gives a closed expression that recovers the zero-temperature result and vanishes throughout the entanglement-breaking region. It improves established benchmarks over broad parameter ranges, while the exact entanglement of the generalized resources remains open. Both results admit refinements under an average-excitation constraint.
