This, in turn, opens the possibility of new quantum- and quantum-inspired solutions to a variety of problems that frequently occur in practical applications. In particular, MOQA can handle various types of routing and partitioning problems, as well as inequality-constrained binary optimization problems.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Egginger, Kristina Kirova, Sonja Bruckner, Stefan Hillmich, Richard Kueng

item.title: Secure PAC Learning: Sample-Budget Laws and Quantum Data-Path Admissibility
item.description: arXiv:2511.02479v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Security in machine learning is fragile when data are exfiltrated or perturbed, yet existing frameworks rarely connect data-path security to learnability. In this work, we develop an operational theory of secure learning grounded in the probably-approximately-correct (PAC) viewpoint. An explicit stopping time combines the event that a trained hypothesis attains a target accuracy with the event that a run-based validation gate halts within a finite sample budget. We derive a closed-form sufficient budget requirement for this joint PAC-within-budget guarantee under an admissible random-classification-noise channel. We then specialize the construction to a BB84-like quantum label path. Under the stated ideal single-qubit, authenticated-classical-channel, memoryless, basis-symmetric, collective-attack, asymptotic, and one-way-reconciliation assumptions, the standard Holevo bound gives the protocol-specific information-advantage criterion $1-2h(\eta) > 0$, with the threshold $\eta_{\mathrm{BB84}} \simeq 0.11$. The quantum layer is not invoked to reduce distribution-free PAC sample complexity; rather, it turns a designer-chosen classical noise tolerance into a physically testable, protocol-dependent security condition by linking information acquisition to observable disturbance. Below the threshold, the PAC and information-advantage conditions provide complementary statistical and physical guarantees; at or above it, the present protocol and proof no longer certify the latter. Basis sifting is incorporated explicitly in the conversion from sifted-sample budgets to expected raw channel uses.
item.dc:creator: Jeongho Bang

item.title: Addressable gate-based logical computation with quantum LDPC codes
item.description: arXiv:2511.06124v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum computing relies on quantum error correction for high-fidelity logical operations, but scaling to achieve near-term quantum utility is highly resource-intensive. High-rate quantum LDPC codes can reduce error correction overhead, yet realizing high-rate fault-tolerant computation with these codes remains a central challenge. Lattice surgery remains the main approach for addressable logical computation but at a cost of $\mathcal{O}(d)$ time overhead. Other approaches rely on low-rate code switching methods or high space overhead homomorphic CNOT. In this work, we introduce a gate-based protocol for addressable single- and multi-qubit Clifford operations on individual logical qubits encoded within one or more quantum LDPC codes. Our scheme leverages logical transversal operations via an auxiliary -- a Bacon-Shor code or an unrotated surface code -- to perform logical operations with constant time overhead enabled by teleportation. We demonstrate the implementation of an overcomplete logical Clifford gate set and perform numerical simulations to evaluate the error-correction performance of our protocol. Additionally, our scheme can also realize any joint Pauli product measurement natively. Finally, we observe that our scheme can be integrated with magic state cultivation protocols to achieve universal, gate-based, and fully addressable quantum computation.
item.dc:creator: Laura Pecorari, Francesco Paolo Guerci, Hugo Perrin, Guido Pupillo

item.title: Local causal consistency as a foundational principle for indefinite causal order
item.description: arXiv:2512.08635v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum processes with indefinite causal order challenge the description of physical experiments as globally ordered networks while retaining causality within each local laboratory. Whether and how this local causal requirement constrains the information flow in such quantum processes remains unclear. Here we formalize the principle of local causal consistency through experiments in which each laboratory performs two sequential operations and may use the earlier outcome to choose the later operation. The principle is equivalent to a set of parity-erasure conditions: the joint earlier outcomes for any set of laboratories reveal no information about the parity of the corresponding independent, uniformly random binary settings. We show that these conditions precisely characterize, via local process tomography, the multipartite channels representing valid quantum processes; characterize classical process-matrix correlations through local readout of outcome tables; and, together with the gentle-measurement property, constrain general quantum correlations with indefinite causal order. Moreover, these results extend naturally to a vast class of theories beyond quantum theory. Our findings provide an operational account of how causality within local laboratories shapes indefinite causal structure and the correlations it supports, revealing a fundamental constraint on information exchange through indefinite causal structure.
item.dc:creator: Zixuan Liu, Ognyan Oreshkov

item.title: Spin-1 quantum annealing with anisotropy-controlled intermediate-state pathways
item.description: arXiv:2512.23469v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum annealing offers a promising strategy for solving complex optimization problems by encoding the solution into the ground state of a problem Hamiltonian. While most implementations rely on spin-$1/2$ systems, we explore the performance of quantum annealing on a spin-$1$ system where the problem Hamiltonian includes a single ion anisotropy term of the form $D\sum (S^z)^2$. Our results reveal that for a suitable range of the anisotropy strength $D$, the spin-$1$ annealer reaches the ground state with higher fidelity. We attribute this performance to the presence of the intermediate spin level and the tunable anisotropy, which together enable the algorithm to traverse the energy landscape through smaller, incremental steps instead of a single large spin flip. This mechanism effectively lowers barriers in the configuration space and stabilizes the evolution. These findings suggest that higher spin annealers offer intrinsic advantages for robust and flexible quantum optimization, especially for problems naturally formulated with ternary decision variables.
item.dc:creator: M. Haider Akbar, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu

item.title: Chip-integrated superconducting gravimetric sensing via flux-mediated transmon mechanical coupling: Theory and device requirements
item.description: arXiv:2601.00425v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Measurements of local gravitational acceleration support geophysics and inertial navigation. We develop a circuit-level model of a chip-integrated superconducting gravimetric sensing head that longitudinally couples a nanomechanical beam in a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) loop to an independently flux-biased transmon. The interaction encodes changes in gravitational acceleration in the qubit Ramsey phase. We derive the phase response and evaluate the quantum Fisher information of the reduced qubit state and the classical Fisher information accessible through Ramsey readout. The model includes qubit relaxation and dephasing, mechanical damping, flux noise, readout infidelity, and cycle overhead. With other model inputs fixed, the competition between phase gain and responsivity-dependent decoherence yields a finite optimal transmon frequency responsivity to mechanical-loop flux. The decoherence model includes dephasing from low-frequency flux noise in the mechanical SQUID loop and coupling-dependent qubit dephasing from the mechanical bath. For the prospective integrated-device parameter set, Ramsey readout at the first mechanical revival gives a conditional projection of the sensing head's sensitivity of $1.1\times10^{-5}$ m s$^{-2}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ at an interrogation time of 10.0 $\mu$s. This estimate uses the single-cycle-equivalent Fisher-information rate for statistically independent cycles. A separate analysis identifies the joint mechanical, circuit, flux-noise, coherence, timing, and readout parameters needed within the model to reach $10^{-6}$-class internal sensitivity. These results specify the design tradeoffs and component requirements for Ramsey gravimetry in the proposed SQUID-transmon electromechanical sensing head.
item.dc:creator: Salman Sajad Wani, Mughees Ahmed Khan, Abrar Ahmed Naqash, Saif Al-Kuwari

item.title: TopoLS: Lattice Surgery Compilation via Topological Program Transformations
item.description: arXiv:2601.23109v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lattice surgery is a leading approach for implementing fault-tolerant logical operations in surface code quantum computing. Current compilers largely treat lattice surgery as a layout problem downstream of a gate-level circuit; this circuit-centric view hinders a substantial optimization opportunity: lattice surgery computations are topological programs whose semantics are determined by connectivity, so different concrete space-time realizations may implement the same computation while offering different space-time volumes. Circuit-centric compilers, however, commit to fixed realizations throughout the program. We tackle this problem by presenting TopoLS, a topology-centric compiler that uses ZX diagrams as the intermediate representation (IR) for automated lattice surgery compilation. Compiler transformations on this graph preserve its semantics, and the backend must produce a valid pipe diagram, i.e., a 3D space-time layout of the lattice surgery program, with the same semantics. TopoLS first simplifies the graph and slices it into layers, and then uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to place the graph's nodes as cubes in a 3D grid and to route its edges as pipes. To scale to large circuits, TopoLS partitions the graph so that each search step routes a bounded number of connections. Across evaluated benchmarks, TopoLS reduces space-time volume by 46% on average over prior circuit-centric compilers, with improvements ranging from 25% to 90%, while exhibiting strong empirical scalability on large benchmark families.
item.dc:creator: Junyu Zhou, Yuhao Liu, Ethan Decker, Justin Kalloor, Mathias Weiden, Kean Chen, Costin Iancu, Gushu Li

item.title: Sublinear Time Quantum Algorithm for Attention Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2602.00874v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given the query, key and value matrices $Q, K, V\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, the attention module is defined as $\mathrm{Att}(Q, K, V)=D^{-1}AV$ where $A=\exp(QK^\top/\sqrt{d})$ with $\exp(\cdot)$ applied entrywise, $D=\mathrm{diag}(A\mathbf{1}_n)$. The attention module is the backbone of modern transformers and large language models, but explicitly forming the softmax matrix $D^{-1}A$ incurs $\Omega(n^2)$ time, motivating numerous approximation schemes that reduce runtime to $\widetilde O(nd)$ via sparsity or low-rank factorization. We propose a quantum data structure that approximates any row of $\mathrm{Att}(Q, K, V)$ using only row queries to $Q, K, V$. Our algorithm preprocesses these matrices in $\widetilde{O}(\epsilon^{-1} n^{0.5} (s_\lambda^{3} + s_\lambda^{2} d + d) + \epsilon^{-2} s_\lambda d)$ time, where $\epsilon$ is the target accuracy and $s_\lambda$ is the $\lambda$-statistical dimension of the exponential kernel defined by $Q$ and $K$. Each row query can be answered in $\widetilde{O}(s_\lambda^2 + s_\lambda d)$ time. If every row sum of $A$ exceeds $\epsilon\|A\|+\lambda\sqrt n$, then with probability $1-1/\mathrm{poly}(n)$ the answers have Frobenius-norm error $O(\beta\|D^{-1}\|(\epsilon\|A\|_F+\lambda\sqrt n)\|V\|_F)$. Here $\beta=(1-(\epsilon\|A\|+\lambda\sqrt n)\|D^{-1}\|)^{-1}\geq 1$ is close to $1$ when every row sum is much larger than $\epsilon\|A\|+\lambda\sqrt n$. To our knowledge, this is the first quantum data structure that approximates rows of the attention matrix in sublinear time with respect to $n$. Our approach relies on a quantum Nystr\"om approximation of the exponential kernel, quantum multivariate mean estimation for computing $D$, and quantum sampling of the rows of $V$ by their squared norms, with a median over independent samples, for the multiplication with $V$.
item.dc:creator: Zhao Song, Jianfei Xue, Jiahao Zhang, Lichen Zhang

item.title: Gradually opening Schr\"odinger's box reveals a cascade of sharp dynamical transitions
item.description: arXiv:2602.02672v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum mechanics predicts that unobserved systems may exist in a superposition of states, yet measurement produces definite outcomes, a tension at the heart of the quantum-to-classical boundary. How the transformation between these opposing regimes unfolds as observation strength increases has remained experimentally elusive. Here, by continuously tuning the measurement strength on a superconducting qubit, we reveal that measurement-dominated dynamics emerge not gradually but through multiple sharp transitions marked by the halting of coherent oscillations, state freezing near an attracting state, and the onset of quantum Zeno dynamics. Decoherence, rather than washing out this structure, reshapes it, reordering the transitions and decoupling signatures that coincide in idealised models. These results establish that the passage from quantum dynamics to measurement-dominated behaviour unfolds through a sequence of distinct transitions governed by the interplay between observation and environment.
item.dc:creator: Barkay Guttel, Danielle Gov, Noam Netzer, Uri Goldblatt, Sergey Hazanov, Lalit M. Joshi, Alessandro Romito, Yuval Gefen, Parveen Kumar, Kyrylo Snizhko, Fabien Lafont, Serge Rosenblum

item.title: Intractability of Witnessing an Entangled Measurement Device Independently
item.description: arXiv:2602.15199v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Protocols have been previously proposed to certify that a measurement is entangled in a fully device-independent manner. Here, I provide models for these protocols in which the claimed measurement is not entangled, and demonstrate it is always possible to displace entanglement from a given measurement to the measured state for a general class of device-independent scenarios. This indicates that no black-box measurement scenario requires a specific chosen measurement to be entangled in order to replicate its behavior, which is relevant to our fundamental understanding of this phenomenon and how to witness it.
item.dc:creator: Peter Bierhorst

item.title: Landscape-Similarity-Guided Optimization in Divide-and-Conquer QAOA
item.description: arXiv:2602.21689v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Divide-and-conquer strategies mitigate hardware constraints for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices by partitioning large interaction graphs into smaller, hardware-compatible sub-problems. However, this approach introduces a severe classical training bottleneck: a decomposition across $m$ boundary nodes generates $2^m$ distinct sub-problems that typically require independent optimization. In this work, we quantify correlations between reduced QAOA energy landscapes using a landscape-overlap measure $q$ and Pearson correlation $r$, and investigate their usefulness for parameter transfer. For $p=1$ on the studied long-range percolation graphs with $L=50$--$400$, the displayed $q(s)$ curves cross near $s\approx0.6$. This observation on finite systems does not establish a thermodynamic phase transition. Exploiting these correlations, we introduce Doubly Optimized QAOA (DO-QAOA), which fully optimizes one representative reduced instance and transfers its parameters to the remaining frozen assignments, with target-specific refinement when required. We evaluated DO-QAOA on more than 6,000 circuits under the realistic noise model, DO-QAOA uses approximately $285$--$386\times$ fewer quantum shots and has approximately $6.5$--$23.9\times$ shorter runtime than FrozenQubits, with equal or lower dataset-averaged Approximation Ratio Gap (ARG).
item.dc:creator: Sokea Sang, Leanghok Hour, Sanghyeon Lee, Aniket Patra, Hee Chul Park, Moon Jip Park, Youngsun Han

item.title: How to find expressible and trainable parameterized quantum circuits?
item.description: arXiv:2603.14451v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Whether parameterized quantum circuits (PQCs) can be systematically constructed to be both trainable and expressive remains an open question. Highly expressive PQCs often exhibit barren plateaus, while several trainable alternatives admit efficient classical simulation. We prove that deciding whether a PQC family exhibits a barren plateau is undecidable in general. However, we derive a practical finite-sample, dimension-independent concentration bound for estimating the variance of a PQC cost function, yielding explicit trainability guarantees. Across commonly used ans\"atze, we observe an anticorrelation between trainability and expressibility, consistent with theoretical insights. Building on this observation, we propose a property-based ansatz-search framework for identifying circuits that combine trainability and expressibility. We demonstrate its practical viability on a real quantum computer and apply it to variational quantum algorithms. We identify quantum neural network ans\"atze with improved effective dimension using over six times fewer parameters, and for VQE on $\mathrm{H}_2$ we achieve UCCSD-like accuracy at substantially reduced circuit complexity.
item.dc:creator: Peter R\"oseler, Dennis Willsch, Kristel Michielsen

item.title: Characterizing entanglement dynamics in QED scattering processes
item.description: arXiv:2604.10136v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the entanglement among helicity degrees of freedom in quantum electrodynamics (QED) scattering processes at fixed momentum, modeled as quantum maps whose spectral structure determines the associated entanglement dynamics. We show that, for fermion-fermion scatterings, parity invariance preserves maximal entanglement and generically leads to entanglement saturation under iterations of the maps. The structure of the maps also provides an accurate description of the entanglement dynamics in processes involving both fermions and photons.
item.dc:creator: Massimo Blasone, Silvio De Siena, Gaetano Lambiase, Bruno Micciola, Kyrylo Simonov

item.title: Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution with Majorana Memories
item.description: arXiv:2604.11442v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) certifies secrecy from Bell nonlocality and has been demonstrated with ions, atoms, and photons. Majorana parity qubits are proposed as network memories, but their operations and noise have not been connected to device-independent security. We show that Clifford-only Majorana operations cannot violate the CHSH inequality on a heralded pair, so a node needs a non-Clifford resource, which we confine to one party's test rounds. Because quasiparticle poisoning flips the total island parity, a parity flag read before the inputs are drawn preserves device independence and turns the poisoning distance cutoff into a rate penalty; flag errors restore part of the loss in proportion to the miss probability. We derive closed-form Bell statistics for realistic heralding and anisotropic Majorana noise, instantiate a block-based finite-size key length, and find that 2025 tetron prototypes cannot yet certify a key. We identify the hardware milestones that would.
item.dc:creator: Noureldin Mohamed, Saif Al-Kuwari

item.title: Uncertainty Relations and Quantum Speed Limits for Lattice-Regularized Fractional Kinetic Operators
item.description: arXiv:2604.24791v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a ``hybrid'' kinetic operator on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ that combines a lattice-regularized momentum, with lattice constant $a$, and a fractional (L\'evy-type) power $\alpha\in(1,2]$. It is a bounded Fourier multiplier whose symbol is a fractional power of the central-difference Laplacian symbol; equivalently, it is a long-range hopping model with algebraically decaying hops. We prove that the kinetic operator is bounded and self-adjoint with purely absolutely continuous spectrum $[0,E_{\max}]$ (for every $\alpha\in(0,2]$), and that $\hat K+V$ is self-adjoint on $\mathcal D(V)$. The main new technical result is an exact position--momentum commutator with domain control for the singular multiplier it produces when $\alpha\in(1,2)$, and the resulting Robertson-type uncertainty relation together with its joint weak-lattice, weak-fractionality expansion. For $\alpha=2$ the uncertainty relation reduces to a known lattice result, which we attribute. For quantum speed limits we recall the bandwidth bound $\tau_\perp\ge\pi\hbar/E_{\max}$, a direct consequence of the Mandelstam--Tamm bound, and evaluate the Mandelstam--Tamm and Margolus--Levitin bounds for Gaussian states in closed form, including their crossover as a function of $\alpha$. To leading order the lattice reduces the energy variance of a Gaussian state and therefore raises the Mandelstam--Tamm bound; the effect of the fractional order is controlled by the width of the state relative to a reference momentum $p_0$ through an explicit crossover width $\sigma_*$. For $\hat H=\hat K-F\hat x$ we show that $\ave{\hx}(t)$ is exactly periodic for every state, and discuss ion-chain realizations.
item.dc:creator: M. W. AlMasri

item.title: Semiclassical Ehrenfest paths in open quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.27328v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the semiclassical Ehrenfest trajectories in open quantum systems. Using the Fokker--Planck equation for the Gaussian mixing measure, we embed the generalized Ehrenfest theorem recently obtained for open quantum systems into this phase-space picture and study the time evolution of the expectations of observables with respect to the Gaussian mixture. We show how the coherent and irreversible contributions are separated in the frictionless harmonic regime relevant to the semiclassical approximation. Our work provides a transparent phase-space interpretation of the emergence of classical trajectories in open quantum dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Kan Guo

item.title: Temporal State Tomography via Quantum Snapshotting the Temporal Quasiprobabilities
item.description: arXiv:2605.02655v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum tomography is a cornerstone of quantum information science, enabling the reconstruction of states and channels from experimental data. Here we introduce a new paradigm, temporal state tomography (TST), for reconstructing quantum processes across multiple times. Our approach is based on temporal quasiprobability distributions (TQDs), which, in the informationally complete setting, provide a complete description of multi-time quantum processes and uniquely determine temporal states. We formulate TST as a unified framework for reconstructing both density operators and quantum channels within a single scheme. We show that any TQD can be obtained via classical post-processing of measurement outcomes generated by a fixed set of quantum instruments, thereby establishing a direct operational route to accessing TQDs experimentally. For informationally complete TQDs, the associated temporal state can be reconstructed via a temporal Bloch-type representation. Leveraging this correspondence, we derive the sample complexity of TST, thereby quantifying its statistical efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Zhian Jia

item.title: Molecular Attoscope: Pulse Shape Spectroscopy of Electronic Coherence
item.description: arXiv:2605.03298v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tracking the coupled motion of electrons and nuclei on their intrinsic timescales is essential to understanding and controlling photochemical transformations. While attosecond techniques have provided unprecedented insight into electronic dynamics, they have largely been restricted to ionic systems, with nuclear motion often neglected or indirectly inferred. Here, we demonstrate a ``molecular attoscope", which uses shaped laser pulses in the deep ultraviolet to perform a coherent measurement of electronic and nuclear dynamics in an entangled wave packet in neutral benzene. This enables us to trace both the 856-attosecond-period electronic motion and the 36-femtosecond-period nuclear motion. We observe electronic coherence persisting over hundreds of optical cycles, modulated by nuclear dynamics. Our holographic approach is general, and lays the groundwork for coherent measurements capable of visualizing the evolution of the coupled electronic-nuclear wave function in real time.
item.dc:creator: Loc Thi-Hoang Ngo, Julia Codere, Javin Ohara, Brian Kaufman, Martin G Cohen, Scott Liguori, Varun Makhija, Tamas Rozgonyi, Philipp Marquetand, Matthew Bain, Brett J Pearson, Ruaridh Forbes, Thomas Weinacht

item.title: An extensive theory of nonlinearly intercoupled pseudomodes for noise model reduction in circuit QED
item.description: arXiv:2605.03946v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamical (cQED) platforms present a persistent modeling challenge: the intrinsic nonlinearity of the Josephson potential couples to a dissipative electromagnetic environment in ways that resist both perturbative treatment and naive Markovian reduction. Standard approaches either scale poorly with system size or absorb undeclared approximations about the noise structure into their master equations. In this work, we generalize Garraway's pseudomode construction to accommodate nonlinearly intercoupled auxiliary modes, providing a nonperturbative and systematically reducible framework for open-system cQED dynamics. The key observation is that pseudomode elimination is not fundamentally tied to linearity but to representability: any eliminated sector whose influence on the retained subsystem admits a rational self-energy can be replaced by a finite set of damped auxiliary modes, independent of the internal nonlinear structure of the retained Hamiltonian. We develop the general theory in the Heisenberg picture via a Dyson equation for the retained-mode Green's function, then demonstrate closed-form elimination for two-, three-, and four-mode Kerr-coupled systems with bilinear exchange and three-wave mixing interactions. The resulting framework substantially reduces the computational overhead of open-system cQED modeling while remaining faithful to the underlying physics, provided the spectral description of the eliminated sector is chosen to match the experimentally measured response functions of the hardware.
item.dc:creator: M. Gabriela Boada G., Nicolas Dirnegger, Andrea Delgado, Prineha Narang

item.title: C-Phase-Aware Compilation for Efficient Fault-Tolerant Quantum Execution
item.description: arXiv:2605.14042v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Achieving practical quantum advantage on fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQC) is fundamentally constrained by significant spatial and temporal overheads required to execute logical operations on physical hardware. Existing compilers fail to exploit the connection between algorithmic structure and fault-tolerant execution primitives, leaving substantial optimization opportunities unrealized. Additionally, they often rely on coarse-grained, slice-based abstractions that ignore microarchitectural overheads, leading to poor resource utilization. We present a microarchitecture-aware compilation approach that integrates algorithmic structure directly with lattice surgery (LS) execution. By leveraging the commutativity of C-Phase operations, the method transforms inherently sequential gate sequences into concurrent multi-target interactions, effectively removing artificial dependencies and exposing significant instruction-level parallelism. To enable this, we design a dynamic, event-driven scheduling strategy that accurately models spatial layout and routing constraints, allowing operations to overlap in time while minimizing contention. Compared to the state-of-the-art compiler, our work achieves up to 24.5$\times$~(geomean~3.7$\times$) reduction in execution time, up to 20.8$\times$~(geomean 2.9$\times$) reduction in space-time volume, and up to 2.7$\times$~(geomean 2.4$\times$) reduction in program-failure probability across three regimes of magic-state production. By co-optimizing the circuit reordering and LS primitives, we make executing fault-tolerant programs faster, cheaper, and more reliable on the same hardware.
item.dc:creator: Dhanvi Bharadwaj, Siddharth Dangwal, Yuewen Hou, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

item.title: Worst-Case Sample Complexity Bounds for Distributed Inner Product Estimation with Local Randomized Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2605.14256v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study distributed inner product estimation for $n$-qubit states using local randomized measurements, for which rigorous worst-case guarantees are less understood. We first reduce the minimax kernel optimization to Hamming-distance kernels. Within this class, unbiasedness fixes a unique kernel. For this kernel under local Clifford sampling, we prove a fourth-moment bound for arbitrary inputs. This yields a worst-case sample complexity upper bound of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{5.25^n})$ copies per party at fixed additive error and failure probability. For the same kernel under local Haar sampling, we prove a local twirling identity that compares its fourth moment with the Clifford fourth moment. A direct bound on the Haar fourth moment shows that $\mathcal(\sqrt{4^n})$ copies per party suffice. We also show that independent single-qubit Pauli shadows have a worst-case sample complexity upper bound of $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{7.5^n})$ for large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Zhenyuan Huang, Kun Wang, Ping Xu

item.title: GeneCS: Synthesizing Resource-Efficient Code Surgery for Arbitrary Quantum Stabilizer Codes
item.description: arXiv:2605.21746v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Efficiently realizing logical operations on general stabilizer codes remains a long-standing challenge in fault-tolerant quantum computing. While code surgery provides a general framework with provable guarantees through joint logical measurements, existing constructions are largely theoretical and incur substantial ancilla overhead in practice. We present GeneCS, a resource-efficient synthesizer of code surgery protocols for arbitrary stabilizer codes, designed for the backend of fault-tolerant quantum compilers. Our approach leverages structure-aware optimizations to eliminate redundancy in graph construction, dynamically balance expansion and congestion, and incorporate code degree constraints. Experimental results show that GeneCS reduces ancillary qubits and checks by over 85\% on average for both single-code and cross-code logical operations, while the optimized constructions exhibit logical-error-rate behavior comparable to the baseline under BP-OSD (belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding). On surface-code stress tests with more than $10^4$ physical qubits, one independent synthesis run takes about one second on average. These results enable practical logical operations and efficient cross-code communication for modern QLDPC (quantum low-density parity-check) codes and heterogeneous code systems.
item.dc:creator: Junyu Zhou, Ali Javadi-Abhari, Gushu Li

item.title: Optimal work extraction in measurement-based quantum Otto engines: Non-adiabaticity and generalized measurements can be beneficial
item.description: arXiv:2605.22583v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Measurement-based quantum heat engines have attracted significant interest as alternatives to conventional thermal engines, as they replace the hot thermal reservoir with quantum measurements, thereby offering greater controllability and simpler implementation. Motivated by these advantages, we investigate a measurement-driven quantum Otto engine with a qubit working substance and study the optimal work extractable from such engines along with the corresponding efficiency, including whether their performance can surpass that of conventional quantum Otto cycles. We analyze the engine in both the infinite-time (adiabatic) and finite-time (non-adiabatic) regimes, considering two distinct implementations obtained through optimization over all projection-valued measurements (PVMs) and over all two-outcome positive operator-valued measurements (POVMs). We show that measurement-based engines can outperform conventional quantum Otto engines within specific parameter regimes and that POVM-based engines can yield higher optimal work extraction than PVM-based ones. Furthermore, by incorporating the thermodynamic cost associated with resetting the auxiliary system required for POVM implementation, we demonstrate that the resulting net work output can still exceed that of PVM-based engines under suitable conditions on the spectral gaps and cold bath temperature. We also identify regimes in which non-adiabatic implementations can yield higher work output and efficiency than their adiabatic counterparts. Our study provides operational guidelines for designing improved measurement-driven quantum Otto engines.
item.dc:creator: Arunabha Das, Sayan Mondal, Debarupa Saha, Ujjwal Sen

item.title: Two Operational Principles Single Out Quantum Theory
item.description: arXiv:2605.23217v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Within a finite-dimensional causal operational-probabilistic theory (OPT), we show that adding just two postulates, local equivalence and purification, suffices to derive the mathematical structure of quantum theory as a whole, without separately assuming quantum rules for states, measurements, composites, or transformations. This resolves the question raised by Chiribella, D'Ariano, and Perinotti (CDP) [Phys. Rev. A 81, 062348 (2010)]. The key step is to establish homogeneity of state cones by combining infinitesimal cone-preserving deformations obtained from these postulates with geometric optimization. CDP purification requires every normalized state to be purifiable and purifications of the same state on any common ancilla to be related by a reversible channel on that ancilla. Our alternative assigns each system one operationally equivalent ancilla that purifies all its normalized states, requiring such reversible equivalence only there. Together with local equivalence, this condition also yields quantum theory.
item.dc:creator: Kenji Nakahira

item.title: Fracton Topological Holography
item.description: arXiv:2606.03582v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topological Holography (TH) is a framework of representing $(d-1)$-dimensional quantum systems with a $d$-dimensional sandwich, consisting of a topological order bulk, a gapped top boundary and a dynamical bottom boundary. Dualities and non-invertible symmetries are represented by the change of top boundary in the TH framework. Existing studies have focused on sandwiches with liquid topological bulk, in this paper we examine some fracton bulks, where we call the framework Fracton Topological Holography (FTH). In particular, the X-cube FTH induces the transverse field plaquette Ising model (TFPIM) version Kramers--Wannier duality, the duality between TFPIM and the two-dimensional $90^\circ$ quantum compass model, and the self-duality of quantum compass model. Haah's code FTH induces a duality of transverse-field generalized Ising models (TFGIMs). The two examples illustrate at least a part of type-I fracton (X-cube) and a part of type-II fracton (Haah's code) models can be used to construct FTH sandwiches. Moreover, we construct an explicit Sequential Quantum Circuit (SQC) switching the top boundary of X-cube sandwich, realizing the TFPIM version KW duality.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Tao Hu, Jie-Yu Zhang, Peng Ye

item.title: Soft information from neural-network logits and correlation-aware matching gaps
item.description: arXiv:2606.08758v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To utilize quantum error-correcting codes, a decoder must infer the logical sector from the measured syndrome. Beyond producing a hard logical decision, some decoders provide soft information that estimates the reliability of that decision. For minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM), a common confidence measure is the complementary gap. Neural-network decoders trained with binary cross entropy naturally output a different confidence score, the logit, whose usefulness for post-selection has already been demonstrated. Here, we compare the logit of a pretrained graph neural-network (GNN) decoder with the complementary gaps of uncorrelated and correlation-aware MWPM, evaluated on identical syndromes from rotated-surface-code memory experiments under circuit-level noise. Incorporating correlations substantially improves matching-based hard decisions, post-selection performance, and calibration, reversing the GNN's advantage at larger code distances while leaving it superior at smaller distance. Exchanging confidence scores shows that their ability to rank logical failures is decoder-relative. An exact-posterior comparison at small distance, together with larger-distance log-loss measurements, further shows that neither score universally provides the closer approximation to posterior soft information. These results reveal that much of the apparent advantage of learned confidence over the standard matching gap arises from correlations omitted by the matching model. Nevertheless, learned logits provide useful soft information without requiring an explicit detector error model or competing-sector matching calculations at inference, offering an alternative where matching-based confidence is costly or unavailable.
item.dc:creator: David Dentelski

item.title: A Dynamical Spacetime Hypothesis for Quantum Entanglement with a Proposed Experimental Test
item.description: arXiv:2606.12457v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum entanglement is a central resource of quantum information science, yet its correlations are ordinarily treated as properties of the quantum state rather than as the outcome of an underlying physical process. Here we explore the hypothesis that these correlations are mediated dynamically by a field propagating locally at finite velocity through an extension of ordinary spacetime, extending the kinematic proposal of Physical Review Research 7, 013261 (2025) to a constrained bulk-field dynamics. Motivated by the constraints imposed by no-signaling on finite-speed hidden-influence models, we consider a warped five-dimensional spacetime with an additional timelike coordinate. We show that the five-dimensional Einstein equations determine the warp factor within a symmetric ansatz, requiring a positive bulk cosmological constant. We show that null trajectories propagating through the additional timelike dimension can project onto arbitrarily large spatial distances at the same ordinary time, although these trajectories do not themselves connect separated points on the brane. Spectral analysis of a minimally coupled bulk scalar reveals a tachyonic four-dimensional continuum. We isolate a normalizable zero-mode sector with stable, retarded effective dynamics in ordinary brane time and obtain an exact solution for a suitably distributed source. Building on these results, we formulate an equal-time contextual coupling and Bohm-Bub-inspired outcome dynamics as additional hypotheses, subject to Born-rule compatibility and multipartite no-signaling. We propose an experiment involving two independently prepared Bell pairs to test for departures from their expected statistical independence. Under specified assumptions on the field covariance and detector response, we derive a conditional inverse-square decay of correlations between the two pairs joint measurement outcomes at large separations.
item.dc:creator: Marco Pettini

item.title: Quantum Otto engine powered by an anisotropic Heisenberg XYZ model under independent local magnetic fields
item.description: arXiv:2606.12877v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a quantum Otto heat engine whose working substance is an anisotropic two-qubit Heisenberg XYZ model. Independent local magnetic fields are used to control each spin individually. The influence of the longitudinal coupling, anisotropy, transverse coupling, and local fields on the net work output and efficiency is systematically examined. Reducing the longitudinal coupling is found to markedly improve both the maximum work and the peak efficiency. The engine performance reaches an optimum at a particular value of the anisotropy parameter. A local work analysis clarifies how work is produced during the cycle. Because of the asymmetric local fields and the intrinsic spin-spin interaction, the two qubits play markedly different thermodynamic roles; the interaction term itself contributes crucially to the total work. We further analyze the variation of quantum entanglement, quantified by concurrence, along the cycle. The results indicate that a pronounced change in entanglement between the hot and cold isomagnetic strokes is closely correlated with the efficiency enhancement. This work offers new insight into the operating principles and control of quantum Otto heat engines.
item.dc:creator: Meiru Li, Maimaitiyiming Tusun, Fang Zhao, Hasiyatihan Abudoula, Tongcheng Wei

item.title: No classical particle limit for massless quanta
item.description: arXiv:2606.14632v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate whether relativistic massless classical particles may emerge as the classical limit of massless quanta. To address this question independently of any specific dynamics, environment, or pointer basis, we develop an axiomatic and operational framework for the coarse-graining approach. In this formulation, a candidate classical phase space is taken as the outcome space of a POVM subject to minimal classicality and covariance requirements. Applying this framework to the Poincar\'e group, we prove a no-go theorem for massless particles: the covariance requirement is incompatible with the operational conditions for classicality. Conversely, we show that the obstruction can be avoided for massive particles by constructing coarse-graining schemes satisfying the minimal classicality requirements. The no-go theorem leaves open field-like limits of massless quanta, such as the emergence of the electromagnetic field, while ruling out classical massless particles, such as classical photons.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Falcone, Simon Fuchs

item.title: Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Mutually Unbiased Operator Frames
item.description: arXiv:2606.23185v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an operator-frame formulation of entropic uncertainty relations in the Hilbert-Schmidt space of operators. For general continuous indexed operator frames, we derive an entropic uncertainty relation for the associated coefficient distributions by combining endpoint norm estimates with Riesz-Thorin interpolation. We then identify a distinguished class of mutually unbiased operator frames, defined through constant-modulus trace overlaps. Under suitable structural conditions, the corresponding coefficient amplitudes are related by a bilinear Fourier transform, leading to a stronger Hirschman-Beckner-type entropic uncertainty relation. As canonical realizations, we consider Weyl displacement operators and Wigner kernels, as well as Cartesian dyadic frames generated by position and momentum eigenstates. These examples recover familiar continuous-variable Fourier dualities while extending entropic uncertainty relations beyond measurement outcomes to operator representations themselves.
item.dc:creator: Jesni Shamsul Shaari, Stefano Mancini

item.title: Electrical-Circuit Simulation of the Uhlmann Phase
item.description: arXiv:2606.24559v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Uhlmann phase extends the concept of geometric phases to mixed quantum states through a parallel-transport condition on purification amplitudes, but its experimental realization has so far required sophisticated quantum platforms with carefully engineered auxiliary degrees of freedom. In this work, we reformulate the Uhlmann parallel-transport condition as a linear matrix differential equation and vectorize it to obtain an effective dynamical generator. This generator can be directly mapped onto the admittance matrix of a classical RC circuit, thereby translating the Uhlmann dynamics into the evolution of circuit node voltages. We illustrate the mapping using the equatorial-loop model and, via a rotating-frame transformation followed by a real decomposition, derive a time-independent, real-valued dynamical system suitable for analog implementation. LTspice simulations of the resulting active RC network faithfully reproduce the Uhlmann geometric phase and its topological transition at the critical purity, demonstrating that classical electrical circuits offer a simple and accessible platform for probing mixed-state geometric phases.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Huan Huang, Yu Wang, Jia-Chen Tang, Xu-Yang Hou, Hao Guo

item.title: Unbiased Estimation of Conditional Covariance for Quantum Optomechanics
item.description: arXiv:2607.06431v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Continuous measurements can prepare macroscopic mechanical oscillators in conditional quantum states, but their covariance is difficult to verify. For each quadrature, the conventional retrodictive estimator is unbiased exactly when the conditional and future-likelihood variances are equal, and it needs a separate rule for the position-momentum cross covariance. Here, we derive an estimator that recovers all three independent covariance entries using one exact identity for linear-Gaussian models. It combines the forward trajectory, a future-likelihood center, and the smoothed trajectory. Using these three trajectories, we reconstruct the covariance of the center-of-mass motion of a 7.71-mg suspended mirror. This covariance describes a thermally squeezed conditional state with a principal-variance ratio of $4.7\pm0.7$. The reconstructed covariance and the measured bias difference between the conventional and three-trajectory estimators agree with the model predictions within propagated uncertainties. Varying the upper band edge resolves changes in all three covariance entries. For upper edges up to 1 kHz, the measured changes agree with the finite-band predictions. Every experimental record covers only a finite frequency band; these results show how such records can be used to characterize conditional mechanical states and provide a basis for future tests of macroscopic entanglement.
item.dc:creator: Katsuta Sakai, Nobuyuki Matsumoto

item.title: Approximate Virtual Quantum Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2607.21240v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The recovery of quantum information after subsystem loss is a central challenge in quantum information processing. However, some quantum states remain beyond the reach of any recovery strategies. Here we identify the algebraic origin of virtual irrecoverability, the \emph{ghost information}---correlations present in the global state that leave no trace on any accessible subsystem. We introduce a scalar measure to quantify its magnitude and prove a universal error floor below which no virtual recovery map can operate, irrespective of resource investment. In such cases only \emph{approximate} virtual recovery is available. We derive upper and lower bounds on the sampling overhead for approximate virtual recovery. Moreover, we show that conditional mutual information, the standard entropic diagnostic, does not determine the sampling overhead. Our work thus establish an algebraic framework of information recovery beyond entropic criteria.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Liu, Linhan Lin, Ke-Mi Xu

item.title: Quantum States over Spacetime Can Hide Setting-Dependent Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.25899v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Determining whether correlations across quantum events arise from one physical process is essential for interpreting quantum states over spacetime (QSOSTs). Yet separately realizable settings can share the same unconditional QSOST without admitting a common process, because compression hides distinctions between underlying dynamics. Using least positive lifts, we derive an exact joint-domination criterion for conditioned data to admit a common deterministic parent. A reset-dephasing example and a sparse interferometric witness make this obstruction testable under trusted readout assumptions. We further establish a minimum-five-reference theorem: for two laboratories with qubit inputs and outputs, any four fixed local product-unitary reference groups cannot universally identify deterministic processes from exact joint data, whereas a specified set of five suffices. These results establish when reconstructed temporal correlations support interpretation as alternative readouts of one stable quantum process, making preparation-readout separation a testable physical property.
item.dc:creator: Jianqi Sheng

item.title: Later Information Can Outperform Earlier Information in Query-Assisted Quantum State Discrimination
item.description: arXiv:2608.01167v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Classical partial information about the states can increase the success probability in quantum state discrimination. An important aspect is its timing, whether it is given before or after the measurement. One might expect that later information is less useful than earlier information, because earlier information can still be stored and exploited at a later stage. Surprisingly, we show that the classical information can be more useful if it arrives after the measurement. We present a framework for state discrimination in which the sender provides classical information in response to a request from the receiver, which we refer to as a query. In some cases, nonorthogonal states can be perfectly discriminated when the query is allowed to depend on the measurement outcome. We give a general method for finding the optimal strategy in this setting, which turns out to be the standard minimum-error discrimination problem for an auxiliary ensemble. We show that for any number of states greater than two, there exists a qubit ensemble exhibiting an advantage of later information.
item.dc:creator: Hanwool Lee, Teiko Heinosaari

item.title: Nanohertz Loss in a Pendulum for Macroscopic Entanglement under Structural Damping
item.description: arXiv:2608.02462v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pendulums are attractive for macroscopic quantum control because gravitational dissipation dilution lowers the modal loss, while the $1/f$ force noise of structural damping allows nearly lossless trapping to suppress the noise at an upshifted resonance. The same $1/f$ spectrum, however, produces a low-frequency tail that penalizes entanglement. To overcome this penalty, we realize a 7-mg pendulum suspended by a stepped fused-silica fiber. Ring-down measurements give an energy-decay rate $\Gamma/2\pi=361(39)$ nHz at the bare resonance $\omega_0/2\pi=2.63$ Hz. The reduction in $\omega_0\Gamma$ relative to the previous uniform suspension more than offsets the penalty. Although both suspensions support entanglement in the error-free model, only the stepped one allows robust verification in the multimode model with experimental uncertainties.
item.dc:creator: Azusa Sawada, Hina Nakano, Kanta Watanabe, Gaku Ohashi, Shota Okumura, Nobuyuki Matsumoto

item.title: Fidelity-Based Robustness Margins for Quantum Control
item.description: arXiv:2608.03698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop certified lower bounds on structure-specific fidelity-threshold robustness margins for finite-dimensional closed quantum systems under piecewise-constant coherent control. A scalar physical parameter may perturb the drift, a control Hamiltonian, or another declared Hamiltonian component across the control horizon. A differential sensitivity bound for the trace-amplitude gate fidelity yields a threshold-dependent Lipschitz constant on the nominal connected safe parameter component and hence a certified finite perturbation radius. Recentering this certificate produces an iterative one-dimensional method whose finite runs return lower bounds on the distance to the first threshold contact. The fidelity may touch the threshold without falling below it. A three-qubit gate-control example shows that the returned bounds vary by up to a factor of three across controllers of comparable nominal fidelity and contain structure-dependent information not captured by nominal differential sensitivity alone.
item.dc:creator: S. P. O'Neil, F. C. Langbein, C. A. Weidner, E. A. Jonckheere, S. Schirmer

item.title: Spin-coherent quantum designs
item.description: arXiv:2608.11310v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coherent states bridge the gap between quantum and classical physics, but their overcomplete and nonorthogonal nature makes it difficult to identify finite sets that represent spin observables exactly. Finite spin-coherent tomography and discrete coherent-state operator bases already exist. Here we address a more specific problem: preserving the canonical contravariant-symbol representation. For a spin-$J$ system, the canonical finite coherent-state formula reconstructs every operator in the rank-$S$ irreducible tensor sector exactly if and only if the sampling directions form a spherical $(2J+S)$-design and the corresponding coherent-state projectors then form a spin-coherent quantum design. We also give an explicit Gauss-Legendre construction which leads to weighted spherical designs. These results provide a systematic way to determine spin-operator moments from finite coherent-state POVMs without full state tomography, with practical protocols for polarimetry and magnetometry. Presented construction can be extended to other compact symmetry groups.
item.dc:creator: Marcin Rudzi\'nski, Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andrei B. Klimov, Luis L. S\'{a}nchez-Soto, Karol \.Zyczkowski

item.title: Micromotion and topological constraints on Floquet-state quantum geometry
item.description: arXiv:2608.13649v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The quantum geometry of Floquet-Bloch states in periodically driven crystals evolves throughout each drive cycle. We show that Floquet topology and micromotion constrain this evolution. Using a projector formulation that separates stroboscopic and micromotion contributions, we bound the deviation of the integrated quantum metric of any Floquet-band subspace from its stroboscopic value and derive a geometric speed limit on its evolution. In chiral Floquet systems, these bounds extend the topological lower bounds set by the $0$- and $\pi$-gap invariants at two symmetry-selected times into finite intervals of the drive, a dynamical topological obstruction. When both invariants are nonzero, it can force a minimum intra-period change in the metric, driven by micromotion. Because the integrated metric is a periodic lower bound on the total spread of time-evolved Wannier functions, such a change can make this spread breathe. An exactly solvable driven spin chain realizes this obstruction and further hosts a flat-band point where each band's metric equals the breathing of its compact localized state. This equality provides a direct geometric characterization of local micromotion, accessible through local spin correlators.
item.dc:creator: Arpit Raj, Johannes Mitscherling, Bj\"orn Trauzettel

item.title: High-Harmonicity Planar Penning Traps for Single-Electron Qubits
item.description: arXiv:2608.17984v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a detailed account of the design choices required for planar Penning traps that feature a highly harmonic confining potential. High harmonicity is indispensable for a number of applications, particularly for confinement of single electrons as qubits in quantum-information processing. The present work extends previous studies [J. Goldman and G. Gabrielse, Phys. Rev. A 81, 052335 (2010)] by a fully analytic treatment of finite electrode gaps and their relevance for small traps on the millimeter size scale and below, when relative gap sizes are non-negligible. We derive the overall trap potential with a particular focus on different models of finite-gap potentials and show how to find the optimum trap geometry and electrode voltages to minimize anharmonicities. The analytic calculations are compared with detailed finite-element simulations.
item.dc:creator: Kedar Mal, A. N. Agnihotri, Sugam Kumar, Wolfgang Quint, Manuel Vogel

item.title: Robust Quantum Key Distribution Arbitrarily Close to Local Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2608.22603v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, Wooltorton et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210802 (2024)] and Farkas [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210803 (2024)] have exhibited the mismatch between Bell inequality violations and their cryptographic application in device-independent quantum key distribution, by showing that arbitrarily close to the set of local behaviours there exist quantum correlations guaranteeing a constant rate of secret key. While these results require correlations attaining the maximum quantum value of a suitable Bell observable (aka the Tsirelson bound) and rely on a kind of ideal self-testing of a maximally entangled state and associated Bell measurement, here we show that the effect is robust: for every one of the Bell inequalities considered by Wooltorton \emph{et al.}, a constant rate of secret key ensues if the observed Bell violation is sufficiently close to the respective Tsirelson bound. For these and also the Bell inequalities of Farkas, we furthermore present numerical results based on semidefinite relaxations of the minimum min-entropy consistent with a certain Bell violation, which demonstrate that small but nonzero key rates can be guaranteed (in principle) by practical and efficient means.
item.dc:creator: Hari Krishnan SV, Andreas Winter

item.title: The inverse eigenvalue problem for Partial Transposes of Two-Qubit States and Sharp Entanglement Bounds from Their Low-order Moments
item.description: arXiv:2608.29068v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The negativity of a finite-dimensional bipartite state $\rho$ can be determined without full state tomography by measuring sufficiently many partial-transpose (PT) moments on multiple copies of $\rho$. When the available copies allow only low-order PT moments to be estimated reliably, how tightly do these moments bound the negativity? For two-qubit states, we answer this question by solving the inverse eigenvalue problem for their partial transposes: an ordered eigenvalue list $(x,y,z,-q)$, with $x\ge y\ge z\ge0$, $q>0$, and $x+y+z-q=1$, occurs as the spectrum of $\rho^{\Gamma_B}$ for some two-qubit state $\rho$ if and only if $q\le y$ and $qy\le xz$. The quantum steering ellipsoid of the $X$ state constructed to prove sufficiency gives a geometric interpretation of the two equality cases. We use these inequalities to determine the exact range of negativity compatible with the two lowest nontrivial PT moments, $p_2=\mathrm{Tr}[(\rho^{\Gamma_B})^2]$ and $p_3=\mathrm{Tr}[(\rho^{\Gamma_B})^3]$. We also compare our sharp negativity bounds with estimates from several existing methods and quantify how much the inverse eigenvalue constraints narrow the negativity interval as a function of $p_3$ at fixed $p_2$. Beyond negativity, we extend this approach to derive attainable bounds for the maximal CHSH value and directional coherent information at fixed $p_2$ and $p_3$. Our result establishes the strongest possible bounds on the negativity of an unknown two-qubit state from just two experimentally accessible PT moments, and shows the potential for obtaining similarly sharp bounds from low-order PT moments by solving the corresponding inverse eigenvalue problem for higher-dimensional bipartite states.
item.dc:creator: Ruoting Dou, Shengjun Wu, Zeng-Bing Chen

item.title: Coherent Floquet quantum reservoirs for molecular property prediction
item.description: arXiv:2609.11071v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses observables of a driven quantum system to make predictions from a sequence of inputs. The robust subharmonic response of discrete time crystals (DTCs) has motivated their use as quantum reservoirs. Here we develop a DTC-QRC architecture for molecular property prediction in which successive graph events or surface-hopping frames drive a fixed Floquet reservoir. An adjustable reset probability controls how long earlier inputs influence the state, and measurements of the final polarizations and pair correlations yield a feature vector of fixed dimension. Weak reset favors classification of inhibitor activity and blood-brain barrier penetration from long graph prefixes, whereas forecasting electronic gaps in ethene favors greater weight on recent nuclear motion. With nonlinear decoding, DTC-QRC outperforms an echo-state network on these tasks at matched input lengths and readout widths. For gap forecasting with this decoder and final-state readout, the dissipative reservoirs share a low-error drive window near the DTC transition reported for related spin chains. Dephasing lowers prediction performance in both molecular applications. In six-qubit classification without programmed reset on the Quafu superconducting quantum cloud platform, pair correlations retain more of their noise-free predictive power toward the DTC side, and the full readout performs best near the transition among the drives tested. The architecture provides a common framework for molecular screening and time-resolved property prediction using quantum reservoir computing.
item.dc:creator: Luofei Wang, Da Zhang, Congren Wang, Yiming Li, Yuxiao Yang, Xuan Zhang, Xuefeng Cui, Zhang-Qi Yin

item.title: Coherence-generating power deviation: Fluctuations and input selectivity beyond average coherence generation
item.description: arXiv:2609.19046v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coherence-generating power (CGP) tells how much coherence a quantum process produces on average from incoherent inputs, but an average can hide where that coherence comes from. We introduce the coherence-generating power deviation (CGPD), the standard deviation of the generated Hilbert--Schmidt coherence over the uniform simplex of incoherent states. CGPD turns coherence generation into a landscape: a small value signals robust production across input populations, whereas a large value reveals selective conversion of particular population imbalances. By representing unitary coherence generation as a quadratic response on population space, we obtain exact first and second moments in arbitrary finite dimension. We prove that every nontrivial unitary generator must fluctuate, and we separate this unavoidable isotropic fluctuation from excess anisotropy. The resulting distinction between average strength and input selectivity has direct consequences for benchmarking, reliability guarantees, input-ensemble susceptibility, and four-copy measurement protocols; it also extends naturally to unital quantum channels. Matched quantum-walk and quasiperiodic-transport examples show that topology and localization can leave CGP unchanged while substantially changing CGPD, revealing structure invisible to the mean alone.
item.dc:creator: Kyoungho Cho, Jeongho Bang

item.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
item.description: arXiv:2609.27537v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that Pauli spectra provide a boundary spectroscope in critical quantum spin chains, resolving microscopic boundary fingerprints and finite responses to physical boundary changes. Universal logarithmic corrections to stabilizer Renyi entropy can remain identical across distinct boundary configurations, while their finite contributions retain information about how the physical boundaries are related. Using critical Ising chains, we demonstrate that suitable combinations of Pauli moments isolate normalization-independent responses to boundary reversal and reveal nonadditive contributions associated with the joint boundary configuration. These responses become analytically accessible through an exact term-by-term correspondence that organizes individual Pauli magnitudes into classical-group statistical structures, with their moments represented by discrete Selberg sums associated with unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic ensembles. In particular, fixed-boundary reversal admits an exact symplectic-character representation, while the same framework provides access to boundary-sensitive behavior at the R\'enyi transition. Our results establish a new connection between nonstabilizerness and boundary criticality through the exact statistical structures of classical-group ensembles.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Rajabpour

item.title: Transverse momentum as the counter-diabatic generator in bent waveguide couplers
item.description: arXiv:2609.36431v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Axis bending of a mode-evolution coupler realizes the counter-diabatic (CD) protocol [Opt. Express 34, 1214 (2026)]. We identify the operator responsible. Rigid lateral displacement is generated by the transverse momentum $\hat p_x$, which in a real two-mode supermode basis is purely $\sigma_y$: exactly the form of the CD term, and the one form that detuning and coupling cannot supply. Equating the two gives the axis slope in closed form, as a ratio of two matrix elements at a single cross section, or $\dot{x}_0=\dot\theta/(\gamma\Delta\beta^{2})$ in coupled-mode variables. It agrees with a numerical offset search to 0.3% and is shown to be the earlier curvature condition viewed from the Kramers-Henneberger frame. Beam propagation simulations compare the bent coupler directly with the unitary-transformation realization built from the same reference structure: the two reach supermode fidelities of 0.994 and 1.000 against 0.886 for the untreated coupler, show comparable bandwidth and fabrication tolerance, and differ inside the device by the frame transformation that relates them.
item.dc:creator: Yu-kai Lee, Shuo-Yen Tseng

item.title: A Few Reveal Many: Constraint-Enhanced Learning of Many-Body Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.39935v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Discovering properties of many-body quantum systems is challenging due to the large number of parameters involved. Here, we show that harnessing fundamental constraints among quantum observables improves quantum learning, enabling the inference of exponentially many quantities from a linear number of direct measurements. We leverage this result to design constraint-enhanced algorithms for evaluating key quantum features such as Entanglement and Magic in 100-qubit simulators. At a fixed number of measurement shots, they achieve up to an 83% reduction in relative error compared with protocols based on constructing "classical shadows" of quantum states. Quantum constraints themselves are therefore a resource for exploring large quantum systems, guiding the allocation of the measurement budget to highly informative observables.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Tedde, Davide Girolami

item.title: Measurement-induced dynamics and emergent symmetries of particles moving in a one-dimensional lattice
item.description: arXiv:2609.40026v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Continuous measurements simultaneously reveal and modify the dynamics of a quantum system. In this work we consider the tunneling motion of particles between the sites of a one-dimensional lattice. We investigate how weak continuous probing of the occupation of a single lattice site induces entanglement and selects definite values for system properties such as wave function parity and permutation symmetry. Our simulations show how continuous measurement can steer systems of two and three particles, with no prior permutation symmetry, into stable bosonic, fermionic and parastatistical symmetry sectors.
item.dc:creator: Salvatore Di Lorenzo, Klaus M{\o}lmer

item.title: Optimal Resource Scaling for Early Fault Tolerant Iterative Quantum Phase Estimation under Cost Error Tradeoffs
item.description: arXiv:2609.40128v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The iterative quantum phase estimation algorithm (IPEA) is better suited for NISQ and early fault-tolerant hardware compared to the original algorithm, which requires the inverse quantum Fourier transform. However, current error mitigation and correction implementations lead to imperfect unitaries, causing erroneous phase feedback in IPEA. To improve the reliability of phase bits is to repeat the k^th iteration for the 2^k-th power of the unitary $N_k^*$ times, followed by a majority decision. However, due to variations in their circuit complexities, different iterations incur varying resource costs ($w_k$) and different per-shot error probabilities ($q_k$). Given tight resource constraints, we ask what the optimal number $\{N_k^*: 1\le k \le L\}$ of shots per bit is: $$\arg \max_{\{N_k\}} \mathbb{P}(\text{all } L \text{ bits correct}) \text{s.t.} \sum_{k=1}^L w_k N_k \le W$$ We construct upper and lower surrogate objectives via concentration and anti-concentration inequalities and prove an asymptotic optimality guarantee for whenever the budget satisfies $W = \sum_{k=1}^L \frac{w_k}{c_k}(\ln L + \omega(1))$, where $c_k=-\ln\left(2\sqrt{\left(1-\frac{q_k}{2} \right) \frac{q_k}{2}}\right)$, which, for $q_k\ll 1$, is proportional to $\ln\frac{1}{q_k}$. Optimizing the tractable lower surrogate yields a true success probability within a $(1-o(1))$ factor of the exact optimum. We observe that when resources are abundant, $W \gg \ln(L)\sum_{k=1}^L \frac{w_k}{c_k}$, optimal allocations are proportional to $\ 1/c_k$. However, when resources are sufficient but not abundant, $(\ln(L)+\omega(1))\sum_k \frac{w_k}{c_k}\le W \le O\left( \ln(L)\cdot \sum_k \frac{w_k}{c_k}\right)$, an additional $-\frac{1}{c_k}\ln\frac{w_k}{c_k}$ correction accounts for error propagation from less-significant to more-significant bits.
item.dc:creator: Mrudula A Mahindrakar, Avhishek Chatterjee

item.title: Four Ways to Stream: Exponential Separations from Random Order and Quantum Memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.06727v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A streaming algorithm can keep classical or quantum memory, and its input arrives in adversarial or random order. Each resource alone is known to beat the basic model exponentially, but it was not known whether random order can help a quantum algorithm. We compare the four models by exponential space separations: every pair is separated on some problem and tied on another, and the two models with one resource each beat each other on different problems, one direction for random inputs, by concurrent work of Bouland, Ding, and Jain. The new phenomenon is that quantum memory and random order together can be exponentially stronger than each alone. We show this on a streaming version of Hidden Matching in which the bits of $x\in\{0,1\}^N$ arrive many times and $m\le\sqrt{N}$ matching requests must be answered on arrival. In random order a quantum algorithm uses $O(\log N\log m)$ space, while classical algorithms need $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$, and quantum algorithms need $\Omega(m)$ when all data comes before the requests. Two properties explain this. Consumability: answering a request destroys the quantum state. Replenishment: the state can be rebuilt from bits that keep arriving, which random order supplies and a data-first order does not. We prove that one quantum message answering $m$ Hidden Matching requests needs $\Omega(m)$ qubits, a conjecture of Gilboa, Jain, and McClean, for $m\le N^{1/2-\delta}$. The rest comes from Noisy Gap Cycle, a problem of Assadi and Sundaresan: tell whether a graph is a union of cycles of length $k$ or $2k$. With long cycles it needs linear space in all four models: we extend their random-order lower bound to quantum algorithms and obtain the first quantum random-order lower bounds for natural graph problems. With short cycles, $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ classical bits suffice in random order, but adversarial order requires polynomial quantum space.
item.dc:creator: Nadezhda Voronova

item.title: Towards the Geometry of Quantum Optical Measurements: Kraus Trajectories in the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg Group Manifold
item.description: arXiv:2610.16512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Since ancient Greek times, geometry has been a method by which humans can make inferences, by the use of similar triangles, about the world far beyond their immediate senses. Similarity plays an equally important role in quantum measurement, except that instead of between triangles on wax tablets and in the sky, the similarity is between the infinitesimal generators of transformation (i.e. rotation, affine canonical transformation) on the page and within the atom. For many quantum optical measurements of a single mode, these generators produce Kraus operators that are contained within a twelve-dimensional Lie group: the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg group manifold ($\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$). In particular, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is general enough to include all diffusively generated 'dyne measurements. In this paper, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ will be used to develop two more general classes of 'dyne measurement: one that interpolates between diffusive homodyne and diffusive heterodyne (``slomodyne'') and one that adds to 'dyne measurements adaptive squeezing and displacement. Our analysis uses an approach known as the Instrument Manifold Program (IMP). In particular, a Harish-Chandra-like decomposition of $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is used to calculate the vielbein transformation from a right-invariant basis to the corresponding coordinate basis, allowing us to universally and autonomously navigate $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ and locate the Kraus-operator of whatever selective process is being considered as it evolves in time according to the measurement record.
item.dc:creator: Tzula B. Propp, Chris S. Jackson

item.title: Quantum-classical algorithm interpolation for spatial search
item.description: arXiv:2610.19255v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum-walk algorithms can quadratically reduce the dependence of spatial search on the classical hitting time $\mathrm{HT}$. Realising this speedup using standard quantum-walk algorithms, however, requires deep coherent circuits, limiting their applicability on near-term and early fault-tolerant quantum devices. We derive a parameterised family of hybrid quantum-classical spatial search algorithms that continuously interpolates between the classical and fully coherent quantum regimes, trading off circuit depth for total query complexity. For any $\gamma\in[0,1]$, our algorithms use circuits of depth $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{\gamma/2})$ and find a marked vertex with constant success probability at total cost $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{HT}^{1-\gamma}\mathsf{S} + \mathrm{HT}^{1-\gamma/2}(\mathsf{U} + \mathsf{C}))$, where $\mathsf{S}$, $\mathsf{U}$, and $\mathsf{C}$ denote the setup, update, and checking costs, respectively. We also derive an optimal continuous depth-query trade-off for fixed-point amplitude amplification, providing a potential building block for other hybrid designs.
item.dc:creator: Diogo Ramos, Duarte Magano

item.title: Local failure of disjoint additivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.25329v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Local Gauss constraints can prevent commuting regional algebras from generating the full algebra assigned to their union. We investigate disjoint additivity on the full magnetic physical subspace of finite-group quantum-double models while keeping the original lattice edge supports fixed. Every finite non-Abelian group exhibits a counterexample on vertex-disjoint regions contained within a contractible disk on a regular square torus. For a fixed eight-edge loop and a specified peripheral contact family, additivity fails if and only if the group is non-Abelian and the selected contacts cover all four interior faces of the loop. Leaving an inner face uncovered restores additivity; for the same loop, so does any second region avoiding the specified testing neighborhood. A peripheral projector restricts the exterior tests on a loop transition, allowing their product to preserve the constraints even when the loop factor does not. We construct union observables that deterministically separate orthogonal relative-sign superpositions that yield identical outcome statistics under every measurement whose effects lie in the generated regional algebra. For a separate wrapping pair, we also determine the complete matrix-block inclusion, identifying missing center-orbit coherences, and construct an independent regular-torus counterexample for the eight-dimensional Kac-Paljutkin Hopf algebra.
item.dc:creator: Yi Liang

item.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
item.description: arXiv:2610.31571v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched R\'enyi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers under conditions on local mixing and local energy estimates. We verify these conditions for one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature and for finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.
item.dc:creator: Hongrui Chen, Zhiyan Ding, Jianfeng Lu

item.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
item.description: arXiv:2611.06761v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.
